title.en: Ethiopian New Year (Enkutatash) and St. Bartholomew the Apostle
title.am: ርእሰ ዐውደ ዓመት (እንቁጣጣሽ) እና ቅዱስ በርቶሎሜዎስ ሐዋርያ

en: Ethiopian New Year (Enkutatash)
Job the Righteous
St. Bartholomew the Apostle
Abba Melyos, Archbishop of Alexandria
Abba Melki of Clysma
Archangel Raguel
am: ርእሰ ዐውደ ዓመት (እንቁጣጣሽ)
ጻድቁ ኢዮብ
ቅዱስ በርቶሎሜዎስ ሐዋርያ
አባ ሜልዮስ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ዘእስክንድርያ
አባ ሚልኪ ዘቊልዝም
ቅዱስ ራጉኤል ሊቀ መላእክት

en: Nativity of the Virgin Mary
Archangel Raguel
St. Elijah the Prophet
St. Eutychus the Apostle
am: ልደታ ለማርያም ድንግል
ቅዱስ ራጉኤል ሊቀ መላእክት
ቅዱስ ኤልያስ ነቢይ
ቅዱስ ኡቲኮስ ሐዋርያ

en: On this day the Church welcomes the New Year. We also remember the healing of Job the Righteous, the martyrdom of St. Bartholomew the Apostle, and the repose of Abba Melyos, Archbishop of Alexandria, and of Abba Melki of Clysma, and we keep the feast of the Archangel Raguel.

Meskerem is the first month of the year in Ethiopia, as it was in ancient Egypt. The day is called Enkutatash, and the Church also calls it Kidus Yohannes, after St. John the Baptist. Each year is named, in turn, after one of the four evangelists: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. The Synaxarium calls this a holy and blessed day, a day to leave old sins behind and to begin new and good works that please God. As St. Paul says, whoever is in Christ is a new creation; the old has passed away, and everything has become new.

On this day, too, Job the Righteous washed in flowing water and was healed of all his sickness. From this came a custom: whenever the year turned and the rivers ran full, people bathed in the new water and asked God to bless them in the year ahead.

St. Bartholomew was one of the Twelve Apostles. When the apostles cast lots to learn where each of them would preach, his lot fell on Elwah, a city in the Egyptian desert. He went there with St. Peter, and they preached and worked wonders that shook the people's hearts. So that they could get into the city, Peter sold Bartholomew as a slave, and he began working in the vineyard of a wealthy official. The vine cuttings he planted burst into flower and bore fruit at once. When the governor's son died, Bartholomew raised him from the dead, and everyone in the city believed.

Later the Lord sent him, with St. Andrew to help him, to a land of very wicked people. They rejected the apostles, despite the many wonders they worked among them. Then God made one of the fearsome dog-faced man-eaters obey the apostles. When the townspeople let wild beasts loose to devour them, he rose up against the beasts and tore them apart, and the whole city was seized with fear. The people believed in Christ and bowed at the apostles' feet; the apostles built them a church, ordained priests for them, and went on their way praising God. Bartholomew then preached Christ in the cities along the coast and taught the people to live in purity. When King Agrippa heard of it, he was furious and ordered him to be put into a sack filled with sand and thrown into the sea. In this way St. Bartholomew completed his martyrdom.

On this day Abba Melyos, Archbishop of the great city of Alexandria, also went to his rest. Counting from St. Mark the Evangelist, he was the third father to lead the Church of Alexandria, and he was appointed in the reign of the Roman emperor Vespasian. For twelve years he faithfully guarded the flock of Christ, and then he departed in peace.

Abba Melki was born in the city of Clysma in Egypt, to a noble and wealthy family. His parents were kind to the poor and loved God, but they had no children. One day his father saw schoolchildren holding writing boards with a prayer asking God to give rest to the souls of the fathers who had taught them, and he grieved: “I have no son. Who will remember me when I die?” He and his wife gave themselves to fasting, prayer and almsgiving, and God gave them twins, a boy and a girl, whom they named Melki and Sefna; Sefna means “dove”. From the age of seven Melki studied the books of the Old and New Testaments. The Holy Spirit rested on him, and instead of playing with other children he read the Scriptures day and night.

When his parents planned to find him a wife, Melki seemed to agree, but in his heart he longed to leave the world. He took gold from his father to give his schoolfellows a feast, sent the servants on ahead, and went off alone. He gave the gold to the poor and his horse to a poor man, keeping nothing but the clothes he wore. Then he went to the monastery of his mother's brother, the holy Abba Awgin, and after three years of testing he became a monk. God gave him the gift of healing. Once, when a great serpent had swallowed a governor's son, Melki prayed in the name of Jesus Christ, and the serpent gave the child back unharmed. In thanks the governor built him a monastery, and hundreds of monks gathered around him there.

The devil, jealous of him, tormented the daughter of the king of Rome, and she kept crying out, “No one can heal me but Melki of Clysma.” The king's soldiers searched until they found him, but he was old and could not travel so far, so he told them, “Go; we will meet at the gate of the city of Rome.” When the time came he prayed, and a cloud carried him to the gate of Rome. He drove the demon out of the king's daughter and refused the gold the king offered him. When he had been a monk for forty-five years, a voice from heaven told him that only three days were left to him. He gathered his monks and urged them to serve God in holy fear. Then the great fathers Abba Antony, Abba Macarius, Abba Shenoute, Abba Bishoy and Abba Pachomius came to receive him, and as the angels sang, his soul left his body. Many wonders took place at his tomb.

This is also the feast of St. Raguel, one of the nine archangels and the angel of light, who revealed to Enoch the burning fire and the judgment in which sinners would perish in the waters of the flood.

May God bless this new year for us in his goodness, and may the prayers of Job the Righteous, St. Bartholomew, Abba Melyos and Abba Melki, and the intercession of the Archangel St. Raguel, be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን አዲሱን ዓመት ትቀበላለች። ጻድቁ ኢዮብ የተፈወሰበትን፣ ቅዱስ በርቶሎሜዎስ ሐዋርያ በሰማዕትነት ያረፈበትን፣ የእስክንድርያው ሊቀ ጳጳሳት አባ ሜልዮስና የቊልዝሙ አባ ሚልኪ ያረፉበትን እናስባለን፤ የሊቀ መላእክት የቅዱስ ራጉኤልንም በዓል እናከብራለን።

መስከረም በኢትዮጵያ፣ እንደ ጥንቷ ግብፅም፣ የዓመቱ የመጀመሪያ ወር ነው። ዕለቱ እንቁጣጣሽ ይባላል፤ ቤተ ክርስቲያንም በመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ ስም ቅዱስ ዮሐንስ ብላ ትጠራዋለች። እያንዳንዱ ዓመት በአራቱ ወንጌላውያን፣ በማቴዎስ፣ በማርቆስ፣ በሉቃስና በዮሐንስ ስም በየተራ ይሰየማል። ስንክሳሩ ይህችን ዕለት ቅድስትና የተባረከች ዕለት ይላታል፤ አሮጌውን ኃጢአት ትተን እግዚአብሔርን ደስ የሚያሰኝ አዲስና በጎ ሥራ የምንጀምርባት ዕለት ናት። ቅዱስ ጳውሎስ እንዳለው በክርስቶስ ያለ ሰው አዲስ ፍጥረት ነው፤ አሮጌው አልፏል፤ ሁሉም አዲስ ሆኗል።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ጻድቁ ኢዮብ በወራጅ ውኃ ታጥቦ ከደዌው ሁሉ ተፈወሰ። ከዚህም የተነሣ ልማድ ሆነ፤ ዓመቱ በተለወጠ ቁጥር ወንዞች ሞልተው ሲፈሱ ሰዎች በአዲሱ ውኃ ይታጠባሉ፤ በሚመጣውም ዓመት እግዚአብሔር እንዲባርካቸው ይለምናሉ።

ቅዱስ በርቶሎሜዎስ ከዐሥራ ሁለቱ ሐዋርያት አንዱ ነው። ሐዋርያት እያንዳንዳቸው የሚያስተምሩበትን አገር ለማወቅ ዕጣ ሲጣጣሉ፣ የእርሱ ዕጣ በግብፅ በረሃ በሚገኘው እልዋህ በሚባል ከተማ ላይ ወጣ። ከቅዱስ ጴጥሮስ ጋር ወደዚያ ሄደው አስተማሩ፤ የሰዎቹንም ልብ የሚያናውጡ ድንቅ ተአምራትን አደረጉ። ወደ ከተማዪቱ መግባት እንዲቻላቸው ቅዱስ ጴጥሮስ በርቶሎሜዎስን እንደ ባሪያ ሸጠው፤ እርሱም በአንድ ባለጸጋ መኰንን የወይን ቦታ ውስጥ መሥራት ጀመረ። የተከላቸው የወይን ቅርንጫፎች ወዲያውኑ አብበው ፍሬ አፈሩ። የአገረ ገዥው ልጅ በሞተ ጊዜ በርቶሎሜዎስ ከሞት አስነሣው፤ የከተማዪቱም ሰዎች ሁሉ አመኑ።

ከዚህ በኋላ ጌታ ቅዱስ እንድርያስን ረዳት አድርጎ በመስጠት እጅግ ክፉዎች ወደሆኑ ሰዎች አገር ላከው። ሰዎቹ ሐዋርያት ብዙ ተአምራትን ቢያደርጉላቸውም አልተቀበሏቸውም። በዚህ ጊዜ እግዚአብሔር ሰው ከሚበሉት አስፈሪዎቹ ገጸ ከልቦች አንዱን ለሐዋርያት እንዲታዘዝ አደረገው። የከተማው ሰዎች ሐዋርያትን ለማስበላት አራዊትን በለቀቁባቸው ጊዜ እርሱ በአራዊቱ ላይ ተነሥቶ ገነጣጠላቸው፤ ከተማውም ሁሉ በፍርሃት ተያዘ። ሰዎቹም በክርስቶስ አምነው ከሐዋርያት እግር በታች ሰገዱ፤ ሐዋርያትም ቤተ ክርስቲያን ሠርተው ካህናትን ሾሙላቸው፤ እግዚአብሔርንም እያመሰገኑ ሄዱ። በርቶሎሜዎስም በባሕር ዳርቻ ባሉ ከተሞች ክርስቶስን ሰበከ፤ ሰዎችንም በንጽሕና እንዲኖሩ አስተማረ። ንጉሥ አግሪጳ ይህን በሰማ ጊዜ እጅግ ተቈጣ፤ በአሸዋ በተሞላ ማቅ ውስጥ አስገብተው ወደ ባሕር እንዲጥሉት አዘዘ። ቅዱስ በርቶሎሜዎስም በዚህ ሰማዕትነቱን ፈጸመ።

በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ የታላቂቱ ከተማ የእስክንድርያ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት አባ ሜልዮስ አረፈ። እርሱም ከወንጌላዊው ከቅዱስ ማርቆስ ጀምሮ ሲቈጠር የእስክንድርያን ቤተ ክርስቲያን የመራ ሦስተኛው አባት ነው፤ የተሾመውም የሮሙ ንጉሥ አስባስያኖስ በነገሠበት ዘመን ነው። ዐሥራ ሁለት ዓመት የክርስቶስን መንጋ በታማኝነት ጠብቆ በሰላም አረፈ።

አባ ሚልኪ በግብፅ ቊልዝም ከተባለች ከተማ ከታላቅና ከባለጸጋ ቤተሰብ ተወለደ። ወላጆቹ ለድሆች የሚራሩና እግዚአብሔርን የሚወዱ ነበሩ፤ ነገር ግን ልጅ አልነበራቸውም። አንድ ቀን አባቱ ያስተማሯቸውን አባቶች ነፍስ እግዚአብሔር እንዲያሳርፍ የሚለምን ጽሑፍ በሰሌዳቸው ላይ የያዙ ተማሪዎችን አየ፤ እርሱም «ልጅ የለኝም፤ ከሞትሁ በኋላ ማን ያስበኛል?» ብሎ አዘነ። እርሱና ሚስቱ በጾም፣ በጸሎትና በምጽዋት ተጉ፤ እግዚአብሔርም ወንድና ሴት መንታ ልጆችን ሰጣቸው፤ ስማቸውንም ሚልኪና ስፍና አሏቸው፤ ስፍና ማለት ርግብ ማለት ነው። ሚልኪ ከሰባት ዓመቱ ጀምሮ የብሉይና የሐዲስ ኪዳን መጻሕፍትን ተማረ። መንፈስ ቅዱስ አደረበት፤ ከልጆች ጋር ከመጫወት ይልቅ ቀንና ሌሊት መጻሕፍትን ያነብ ነበር።

ወላጆቹ ሚስት ሊያጋቡት ባሰቡ ጊዜ ሚልኪ የተስማማ መሰለ፤ በልቡ ግን ዓለምን ትቶ ለመሄድ ይናፍቅ ነበር። ለትምህርት ቤት ባልንጀሮቹ ግብዣ ለማድረግ ከአባቱ ወርቅ ተቀብሎ አገልጋዮቹን ቀድመው እንዲሄዱ ላካቸው፤ እርሱም ብቻውን ተለይቶ ሄደ። ወርቁን ለድሆች፣ ፈረሱንም ለአንድ ድሀ ሰጠ፤ ከለበሰው ልብስ በቀር ምንም አላስቀረም። ከዚያም የእናቱ ወንድም ወደሆነው ወደ ቅዱሱ አባ አውጊን ገዳም ሄደ፤ ሦስት ዓመት ከተፈተነ በኋላ መነኰሰ። እግዚአብሔርም የፈውስ ጸጋ ሰጠው። አንድ ጊዜ ታላቅ ዘንዶ የአገረ ገዥን ልጅ በዋጠ ጊዜ ሚልኪ በኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ ስም ጸለየ፤ ዘንዶውም ሕፃኑን ምንም ሳይጎዳ ተፋው። አገረ ገዥውም በምስጋና ገዳም ሠራለት፤ በዚያም በመቶ የሚቈጠሩ መነኰሳት በዙሪያው ተሰበሰቡ።

ሰይጣንም በእርሱ ቀንቶ የሮምን ንጉሥ ልጅ አሠቃያት፤ እርሷም «ከቊልዝሙ ሚልኪ በቀር የሚፈውሰኝ የለም» እያለች ጮኸች። የንጉሡ ወታደሮች ፈልገው አገኙት፤ እርሱ ግን ሽማግሌ ስለነበረ ያን ያህል መንገድ መጓዝ አልቻለም፤ ስለዚህ «ሂዱ፤ በሮም ከተማ በር እንገናኛለን» አላቸው። ጊዜው ሲደርስ ጸለየ፤ ደመናም ተሸክማ ከሮም ከተማ በር አደረሰችው። ከንጉሡ ልጅ ላይ ጋኔኑን አስወጣ፤ ንጉሡ ያቀረበለትንም ወርቅ አልተቀበለም። ከመነኰሰ አርባ አምስት ዓመት በሆነው ጊዜ ሦስት ቀን ብቻ እንደቀረው የሚነግር ድምፅ ከሰማይ መጣለት። መነኰሳቱን ሰብስቦ እግዚአብሔርን በፍርሃት እንዲያገለግሉ መከራቸው። ከዚያም ታላላቆቹ አባቶች አባ እንጦንስ፣ አባ መቃርስ፣ አባ ሲኖዳ፣ አባ ብሶይና አባ ጳኵሚስ ሊቀበሉት መጡ፤ መላእክትም እየዘመሩ ነፍሱ ከሥጋው ተለየች። በመቃብሩም ብዙ ተአምራት ተደረጉ።
ይህች ዕለት ደግሞ ከዘጠኙ ሊቃነ መላእክት አንዱ የሆነው የብርሃን መልአክ የቅዱስ ራጉኤል በዓል ናት፤ እርሱም ስለሚነድደው እሳትና ኃጥአን በጥፋት ውኃ ስለሚጠፉበት ፍርድ ለሄኖክ የገለጠለት ነው።
እግዚአብሔር ይህን አዲስ ዓመት በቸርነቱ ይባርክልን፤ የጻድቁ ኢዮብ፣ የቅዱስ በርቶሎሜዎስ፣ የአባ ሜልዮስና የአባ ሚልኪ ጸሎት፣ የሊቀ መላእክት የቅዱስ ራጉኤልም ምልጃ ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

am.verse: ስለዚህ፥ ማንም በክርስቶስ ቢሆን ዐዲስ ፍጥረት ነው፤ አሮጌው ነገር ዐልፏል፤ እንሆ፥ ሁሉም ዐዲስ ሆኗል።

title.en: Martyrdom of St. John the Baptist
title.am: የቅዱስ ዮሐንስ መጥምቅ ሰማዕትነት

en: Martyrdom of St. John the Baptist
St. Dasya the Martyr
Saints Didymus and Marina, Martyrs
am: የቅዱስ ዮሐንስ መጥምቅ ሰማዕትነት
ቅዱስ ዳስያ ሰማዕት
ቅዱስ ዲዲሞስና ቅድስት መሪና ሰማዕታት

en: Archangel Uriel
St. Theodore the Martyr
Abba Paul the First Hermit
Abba John the Righteous
am: ቅዱስ ዑራኤል ሊቀ መላእክት
ቅዱስ ቴዎድሮስ ሰማዕት
አባ ጳውሊ ቀዳሜ ገዳማውያን
አባ ዮሐንስ ጻድቅ

en: On this day the Church remembers the martyrdom of St. John the Baptist, and with him the martyrs St. Dasya, St. Didymus and St. Marina.

John, the son of Zechariah the priest, was the prophet who prepared the way for Christ. When King Herod married Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, John fearlessly rebuked him: “It is not lawful for you to marry your brother's wife.” He also reproved the king for the other evil things he did. So Herod had John thrown into prison. Yet Herod was afraid of him, because he knew that John was a righteous and holy man.

On his birthday Herod gave a banquet for the nobles, officials and leading men of Galilee. The daughter of Herodias came in and danced, and she pleased Herod and his guests so much that he swore to give her anything she asked, even half of his kingdom. She went out and asked her mother what she should ask for, and her mother said, “The head of John the Baptist.” The girl hurried back to the king and said, “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter, right now.”

The king was deeply grieved, but because of his oath and the guests at his table, he did not want to refuse her. He sent a soldier, who beheaded John in the prison; they brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and she gave it to her mother. Then the holy head flew up into the air, crying out, “Herod, it is not lawful for you to marry your brother's wife!”, and everyone was seized with great terror. John's disciples came, took his body and buried it. Many years later God revealed his body to St. Athanasius, Archbishop of Alexandria, who kept it with honor until a church could be built for it.

On this day, too, St. Dasya, a soldier from the town of Tayda in Egypt, became a martyr. Arianus, the governor of Antinoe, put him to cruel tortures and then had him beheaded with the sword, and he received the crown of martyrdom in the kingdom of heaven.
We also remember the holy martyrs St. Didymus and St. Marina.
May the prayers and blessings of St. John the Baptist, St. Dasya, St. Didymus and St. Marina be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን የመጥምቁ የቅዱስ ዮሐንስን ሰማዕትነት ታስባለች፤ ከእርሱም ጋር ሰማዕታቱ ቅዱስ ዳስያ፣ ቅዱስ ዲዲሞስና ቅድስት መሪና ይታሰባሉ።

የካህኑ የዘካርያስ ልጅ ዮሐንስ የክርስቶስን መንገድ የጠረገ ነቢይ ነው። ንጉሥ ሄሮድስ የወንድሙን የፊልጶስን ሚስት ሄሮድያዳን ባገባ ጊዜ ዮሐንስ ሳይፈራ «የወንድምህን ሚስት ልታገባ አይገባህም» ብሎ ገሠጸው። ንጉሡ ስለሚሠራቸውም ሌሎች ክፉ ሥራዎች ይወቅሰው ነበር። ስለዚህ ሄሮድስ ዮሐንስን በወኅኒ አሰረው። ሆኖም ጻድቅና ቅዱስ ሰው እንደሆነ ያውቅ ስለነበረ ይፈራው ነበር።

ሄሮድስ በተወለደበት ቀን ለገሊላ መኳንንት፣ ሹማምንትና ታላላቅ ሰዎች ግብዣ አደረገ። የሄሮድያዳ ልጅ ገብታ ዘፈነች፤ ሄሮድስንና እንግዶቹን እጅግ ደስ ስላሰኘች፣ የመንግሥቱ እኩሌታ እንኳ ቢሆን የምትለምነውን ሁሉ ሊሰጣት ማለላት። እርሷም ወጥታ ምን እንደምትለምን እናቷን ጠየቀች፤ እናቷም «የመጥምቁ ዮሐንስን ራስ» አለቻት። ልጅቱም ፈጥና ወደ ንጉሡ ተመልሳ «የመጥምቁ ዮሐንስን ራስ አሁኑኑ በወጭት እንድትሰጠኝ እፈልጋለሁ» አለችው።

ንጉሡ እጅግ አዘነ፤ ነገር ግን ስለ መሐላውና በማዕድ አብረውት ስለ ነበሩት እንግዶች እምቢ ሊላት አልፈለገም። ወታደር ልኮ ዮሐንስን በወኅኒ ውስጥ አስቈረጠው፤ ራሱንም በወጭት አምጥተው ለልጅቱ ሰጧት፤ እርሷም ለእናቷ ሰጠች። በዚያን ጊዜ የቅዱሱ ራስ ወደ አየር በርሮ «ሄሮድስ ሆይ፣ የወንድምህን ሚስት ልታገባ አይገባህም» እያለ ስለ ጮኸ ሁሉም በታላቅ ድንጋጤ ተያዙ። ደቀ መዛሙርቱም መጥተው ሥጋውን ወስደው ቀበሩት። ከብዙ ዘመን በኋላ እግዚአብሔር ሥጋውን ለእስክንድርያው ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ለቅዱስ አትናቴዎስ ገለጠለት፤ እርሱም ቤተ ክርስቲያን እስኪሠራለት ድረስ በክብር ጠበቀው።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ በግብፅ ታዕዳ ከተባለች ከተማ የተገኘው ወታደሩ ቅዱስ ዳስያ ሰማዕት ሆነ። የእንዴና አገረ ገዥ አርያኖስ ጽኑ ሥቃይ አሠቃየው፤ ከዚያም ራሱን በሰይፍ አስቈረጠው፤ እርሱም በመንግሥተ ሰማያት የሰማዕትነትን አክሊል ተቀበለ።
ቅዱሳን ሰማዕታት ቅዱስ ዲዲሞስንና ቅድስት መሪናንም እናስባለን።
የቅዱስ ዮሐንስ መጥምቅ፣ የቅዱስ ዳስያ፣ የቅዱስ ዲዲሞስና የቅድስት መሪና ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: Most certainly I tell you, among those who are born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.

am.verse: እውነት እላችኋለሁ፥ ከሴቶች ከተወለዱት መካከል ከመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ የሚበልጥ አልተነሣም፤ በመንግሥተ ሰማያት ግን ከሁሉ የሚያንሰው ይበልጠዋል።

title.en: The Council of Alexandria and Abba Moses of Scete
title.am: የእስክንድርያ ጉባዔና የሲሐት አባ ሙሴ

en: The General Council of Bishops at Alexandria
Abba Dioscorus the Martyr, Archbishop Dionysius and the Martyrs of Persia
Abba Anbes of Ethiopia
Abba Moses of the Desert of Scete
am: የእስክንድርያው የኤጲስ ቆጶሳት ጠቅላላ ጉባዔ
አባ ዲዮስቆሮስ ሰማዕት፣ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ዲዮናስዮስና የፋርስ ሰማዕታት
ኢትዮጵያዊው አባ አንበስ
የሲሐት በረሃ አባ ሙሴ

en: Presentation of the Virgin Mary
Saints Joachim and Anna
St. Zena Markos
St. Cyril the Pillar of Faith
am: በዓታ ለማርያም ድንግል
ቅዱሳን ኢያቄም ወሐና
ቅዱስ ዜና ማርቆስ
ቅዱስ ቄርሎስ ዓምደ ሃይማኖት

en: On this day the Church remembers the General Council of Bishops held in Alexandria in the days of Archbishop Dionysius. We also remember the martyr Abba Dioscorus, Archbishop Dionysius and the martyrs of Persia, as well as the repose of Abba Anbes of Ethiopia and of Abba Moses of the desert of Scete.

In Abba Dionysius's second year as Archbishop of Alexandria, the bishops met there in a general council. Some wicked men in Arabia were teaching that the soul dies with the body and will be raised with it on the day of the resurrection, and they sent their written teaching to people in Alexandria. Abba Dionysius was deeply grieved. He taught and rebuked them, but they would not listen. So he called the council, debated with them and showed them their error. Satan had blinded them, and they did not repent, so the council condemned them and cut them off from the unity of the Church.

Abba Dionysius also wrote a treatise about these men. He spoke of the greatness of God's love and explained that the soul is spiritual and, like the angels, does not die or perish. When it leaves the body, it is taken to the place its works deserve, to life or to torment. On the day of the Resurrection, at the Creator's command, each soul will be joined to its own body and rise with it.
We also remember the martyr Abba Dioscorus, Archbishop Dionysius and the many martyrs of Persia.
On this day Abba Anbes of Ethiopia, whose name means “lion”, also went to his rest.

When Abba Moses of the desert of Scete became a monk, he left the world and went into the wilderness to live by fasting and prayer. God showed him a grove of olive and palm trees, and at the start of each month he ate a little of the fallen fruit, no more than a small bird would eat. His clothing was woven from palm leaves, and he bore the cold of winter and the heat of summer. Though he could not read, the wild animals came to him and he calmed them, and in times of drought the Holy Spirit showed him what they needed and his prayer brought them rain. He lived this way among the animals for forty-five years.

But Satan was jealous of him. He took the form of a very old monk and came slowly to Moses' cave, and Moses welcomed him in, thinking he was a fellow hermit. The old man said that he had a daughter whom only Moses could marry, and that Moses would bury him and inherit all his gardens. Moses was terrified: “I am a monk. How can I do this?” But the old man pointed to the Scriptures, where Abraham, Moses and David, though righteous, had wives, and so he swayed Moses' heart. Then he showed him a splendid hall with a young woman in it, but when Moses went toward her, a mighty wind threw him backward, and everything vanished.

Hunger drove Moses out of the cave, and Satan met him again, first as an old traveler who led him to a city, and then as a woman who took him into her house, fed him and spoke of marriage. When she saw that his heart leaned toward her, she told him that she was Jewish, and with many tricks she led him on until he denied his faith. Then she took him to a waterless desert, climbed a mountain and changed her shape. “I am Satan, who leads many astray,” she said. “Now you will die in this desert, and your soul will go down to Gehenna.” Then Satan vanished.

Moses could find no road and no water. He threw himself on the ground, scattered dust on his face and wept until he was close to death. The merciful God, who loves mankind, sent an angel to comfort him: “Your sin is forgiven. Within seven days you will go to your rest, and my servant Samuel will bury you.” At once Abba Samuel came and took him to a church hidden in the desert, where the monks gathered; there they found the holy monks celebrating the Eucharist and received Holy Communion with them. Then they went to receive a blessing at the tombs of the saints, and there Moses bowed down and went to his rest. Abba Samuel buried him and wrote the story of his life.
May the prayers and blessings of Abba Dionysius, Abba Dioscorus, Abba Anbes, Abba Moses and the martyrs of Persia be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን በሊቀ ጳጳሳት በዲዮናስዮስ ዘመን በእስክንድርያ የተደረገውን የኤጲስ ቆጶሳት ጠቅላላ ጉባዔ ታስባለች። ሰማዕቱን አባ ዲዮስቆሮስን፣ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ዲዮናስዮስንና የፋርስ ሰማዕታትን፣ እንዲሁም ኢትዮጵያዊው አባ አንበስና የሲሐት በረሃው አባ ሙሴ ያረፉበትን እናስባለን።

አባ ዲዮናስዮስ የእስክንድርያ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት በነበረበት በሁለተኛው ዓመት ኤጲስ ቆጶሳቱ በዚያ ተሰብስበው ጠቅላላ ጉባዔ አደረጉ። በዐረቢያ የተነሡ አንዳንድ ክፉ ሰዎች ነፍስ ከሥጋ ጋር እንደምትሞትና በትንሣኤ ቀን ከእርሱ ጋር እንደምትነሣ ያስተምሩ ነበር፤ ትምህርታቸውንም ጽፈው በእስክንድርያ ለሚኖሩ ሰዎች ላኩ። አባ ዲዮናስዮስ እጅግ አዘነ። በትምህርት አስረዳቸው፤ ገሠጻቸውም፤ ሆኖም ሊሰሙት አልወደዱም። ስለዚህ ጉባዔውን ጠርቶ ከእነርሱ ጋር ተከራከረ፤ ስሕተታቸውንም አሳያቸው። ሰይጣን አሳውሯቸው ስለነበር አልተጸጸቱም፤ ስለዚህም ጉባዔው አወገዛቸው፤ ከቤተ ክርስቲያን አንድነትም ለያቸው።

አባ ዲዮናስዮስ ስለ እነዚህ ሰዎች ድርሳን ጻፈ። በውስጡም የእግዚአብሔር ፍቅር ታላቅ እንደሆነ ተናገረ፤ ነፍስ መንፈሳዊ እንደሆነችና እንደ መላእክት እንደማትሞት፣ እንደማትጠፋም አስረዳ። ከሥጋ በምትወጣበት ጊዜ እንደ ሥራዋ ወደሚገባት ቦታ ትወሰዳለች፤ ይኸውም ወደ ሕይወት ወይም ወደ ሥቃይ ነው። በትንሣኤ ቀን ደግሞ በፈጣሪ ትእዛዝ እያንዳንዷ ነፍስ ወደ ገዛ ሥጋዋ ገብታ ከእርሱ ጋር ትነሣለች።
ሰማዕቱን አባ ዲዮስቆሮስን፣ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ዲዮናስዮስንና በፋርስ የነበሩ ብዙ ሰማዕታትንም እናስባለን።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ስሙ «አንበሳ» ማለት የሆነው ኢትዮጵያዊው አባ አንበስ አረፈ።

የሲሐት በረሃው አባ ሙሴ በመነኰሰ ጊዜ ዓለምን ትቶ በጾምና በጸሎት ለመኖር ወደ በረሃ ገባ። እግዚአብሔር የወይራና የዘንባባ ዛፎች ያሉበትን አትክልት ቦታ አሳየው፤ እርሱም በየወሩ መባቻ ከዛፎቹ ከወደቀው ፍሬ ጥቂት ይበላ ነበር፤ መጠኑም ከትንሽ ወፍ ምግብ አይበልጥም ነበር። ልብሱ ከዘንባባ ቅጠል የተሸመነ ነበር፤ የክረምቱን ቅዝቃዜና የበጋውንም ሙቀት ይታገሥ ነበር። ማንበብ ባያውቅም የበረሃ አራዊት ወደ እርሱ ይመጡ ነበር፤ እርሱም ያረጋጋቸው ነበር፤ ድርቅ በሆነ ጊዜም መንፈስ ቅዱስ የሚያስፈልጋቸውን ይገልጥለት ነበር፤ እርሱም በጸሎቱ ዝናብ ያወርድላቸው ነበር። በዚህ ሁኔታ በአራዊቱ መካከል አርባ አምስት ዓመት አሳለፈ።

ሰይጣን ግን ቀናበት። እጅግ ያረጀ መነኰስ መስሎ ቀስ እያለ እየተራመደ ወደ ሙሴ ዋሻ መጣ፤ ሙሴም እንደ እርሱ በበረሃ የሚኖር ሰው መስሎት ተቀብሎ ወደ ዋሻው አስገባው። ሽማግሌውም ሴት ልጅ እንዳለችውና ከሙሴ በቀር ሊያገባት የሚችል እንደሌለ ነገረው፤ ሲሞትም ሙሴ እንደሚቀብረውና የአትክልት ቦታዎቹን ሁሉ እንደሚወርስ ተናገረ። ሙሴ ደንግጦ «እኔ መነኰስ ነኝ፤ እንዲህ ያለውን ነገር እንዴት ላደርግ እችላለሁ?» አለ። ሽማግሌው ግን ከመጻሕፍት ጠቅሶ አብርሃም፣ ሙሴና ዳዊት ጻድቃን ሆነው ሳሉ ሚስቶች እንደነበሯቸው አሳየው፤ በዚህም የሙሴን ልብ አዘነበለው። ከዚያም ወጣት ሴት ያለችበትን ያማረ አዳራሽ አሳየው፤ ሙሴ ወደ እርሷ ሊሄድ ሲል ግን ብርቱ ነፋስ ወደ ኋላ ጣለው፤ ሁሉም ነገር ጠፋ።

ረኃብ ሙሴን ከዋሻው አስወጣው፤ ሰይጣንም እንደገና አገኘው፤ በመጀመሪያ ወደ አንዲት ከተማ የመራው ሽማግሌ መንገደኛ መስሎ፣ ከዚያም ወደ ቤቷ ወስዳ የመገበችውና ስለ ጋብቻ ያነጋገረችው ሴት መስሎ ተገለጠለት። ልቡ ወደ እርሷ እንዳዘነበለ ባየች ጊዜ አይሁዳዊት መሆኗን ነገረችው፤ በብዙ ተንኰልም እያሳተች ሃይማኖቱን እስኪክድ አደረሰችው። ከዚያም ውኃ በሌለው በረሃ ውስጥ ይዛው ሄደች፤ ተራራ ላይ ወጥታ መልኳን ለወጠች። «ብዙዎችን የማሳት እኔ ሰይጣን ነኝ፤ አሁን በዚህ በረሃ ትሞታለህ፤ ነፍስህም ወደ ገሃነም ትወርዳለች» አለችው፤ ከዚያም ሰይጣን ተሠወረ።

ሙሴ መንገድም ውኃም አጣ። በምድር ላይ ወድቆ በፊቱ ላይ አፈር ነሰነሰ፤ ሊሞትም እስኪቃረብ አለቀሰ። መሐሪው እግዚአብሔር፣ ሰውን የሚወደው አምላክ፣ ራርቶለት መልአክ ላከ፤ መልአኩም ሙሴን «ኃጢአትህ ተሠርዮልሃል፤ በሰባት ቀን ውስጥ ታርፋለህ፤ አገልጋዬ ሳሙኤልም ይቀብርሃል» በማለት አጽናናው። ወዲያውም አባ ሳሙኤል መጥቶ በበረሃ ወደተሠወረች፣ መነኰሳት ወደሚሰበሰቡባት ቤተ ክርስቲያን አደረሰው፤ በዚያም ቅዱሳን መነኰሳት ቅዳሴ ሲያደርሱ አግኝተው ከእነርሱ ጋር ቅዱስ ቁርባን ተቀበሉ። ከዚያም ከቅዱሳን መቃብር በረከት ለመቀበል ሄዱ፤ በዚያ ሙሴ ሲሰግድ ወዲያው አረፈ። አባ ሳሙኤልም ቀብሮት የሕይወቱን ታሪክ ጻፈ።
የአባ ዲዮናስዮስ፣ የአባ ዲዮስቆሮስ፣ የአባ አንበስ፣ የአባ ሙሴና የፋርስ ሰማዕታት ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: Don’t marvel at this, for the hour comes in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice, and will come out; those who have done good, to the resurrection of life; and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.

am.verse: በመቃብር ያሉቱ ሁሉ ድምፁን የሚሰሙበት ሰዓት ይመጣል፤ መልካምም ያደረጉ ለሕይወት ትንሣኤ ክፉም ያደረጉ ለፍርድ ትንሣኤ ይወጣሉና በዚህ አታድንቁ።

title.en: Abba Macarius, Archbishop of Alexandria
title.am: አባ መቃርስ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ዘእስክንድርያ

en: Abba Macarius, Archbishop of Alexandria
Joshua the Son of Nun
The Two Hundred Martyrs of Antioch
am: አባ መቃርስ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ዘእስክንድርያ
የነዌ ልጅ ኢያሱ
የአንጾኪያ ሁለት መቶ ሰማዕታት

en: St. John the Evangelist
St. Andrew the Apostle
St. Sophia and her Daughters
am: ቅዱስ ዮሐንስ ወንጌላዊ
ቅዱስ እንድርያስ ሐዋርያ
ቅድስት ሶፍያ ወአዋልዳ

en: On this day the Church remembers the repose of Abba Macarius, Archbishop of Alexandria. We also remember Joshua the son of Nun and the two hundred martyrs of Antioch.

Macarius was the sixty-ninth archbishop of Alexandria. From his earliest years he gave himself to hard spiritual struggle, and he longed to wear the habit of a monk. So he went up to the monastery of Scete and became a monk in the church of the first Abba Macarius, where he took up the great labors of monastic life. He read the Holy Scriptures constantly and studied their interpretation, he grew strong in righteous deeds, and he was ordained a priest.

When Abba Michael, the archbishop before him, died, the bishops went to the monastery of Scete, together with many learned priests of the true faith. They met with the senior monks of Scete and sat with them for many days, searching for the man who was worthy of this honored office. At last they found that Abba Macarius was the best of all, and they agreed unanimously to appoint him, because many holy monks of Scete testified to his righteousness and his struggles.

They seized him against his will and bound him. Macarius cried out, “I am not fit to be raised to the dignity of archbishop, for my mother married two men.” But he said this only so that they would let him go, and many people testified that his mother had been married to only one man and had lived a pure life. So they did not accept his excuse. They took him to Alexandria and made him archbishop; then they brought him to Misr (Cairo), and in the church of Our Lady the Virgin Mary at Mu'allakah the letter of his appointment was read aloud in Greek, Coptic and Arabic.

In all the years of his office he added to his good works day by day and struggled with all his strength. Every day he taught the people and urged them to live in the fear of God. He gave alms and showed mercy to the poor and needy. He never took anything from the Church's money; on the contrary, he gave a part of the dues paid to him back to the Church and to those in need. After twenty-seven years as archbishop he died in peace, having served and pleased God.
We also remember Joshua the son of Nun, the disciple of Moses.
And we remember the two hundred who died as martyrs in Antioch.
May the prayers and blessings of Abba Macarius, Joshua the son of Nun and the martyrs of Antioch be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን የእስክንድርያው ሊቀ ጳጳሳት የአባ መቃርስን ዕረፍት ታስባለች። የነዌን ልጅ ኢያሱንና የአንጾኪያን ሁለት መቶ ሰማዕታትም እናስባለን።

መቃርስ ስድሳ ዘጠነኛው የእስክንድርያ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ነበር። ከልጅነቱ ጀምሮ ራሱን ለገድል የሰጠ ነበር፤ የምንኵስናንም ልብስ ለመልበስ ይናፍቅ ነበር። ስለዚህ ወደ አስቄጥስ ገዳም ወጥቶ በመጀመሪያው አባ መቃርስ ቤተ ክርስቲያን መነኰሰ፤ በዚያም ታላቅ የምንኵስና ተጋድሎ ጀመረ። ቅዱሳት መጻሕፍትን ሁልጊዜ ያነብ፣ ትርጓሜያቸውንም ይማር ነበር፤ በጽድቅ ሥራም እየበረታ ሄደ፤ ቅስናም ተሾመ።

የቀድሞው ሊቀ ጳጳሳት አባ ሚካኤል ባረፈ ጊዜ ኤጲስ ቆጶሳቱ ወደ አስቄጥስ ገዳም ሄዱ፤ ሃይማኖታቸው የቀና ብዙ ሊቃውንት ካህናትም አብረዋቸው ነበሩ። ከአስቄጥስ ታላላቅ መነኰሳት ጋር ተሰብስበው ለዚህ የከበረ ሹመት የሚገባውን ሰው ሲፈልጉ ብዙ ቀናት ተቀመጡ። በመጨረሻም አባ መቃርስ ከሁሉ የተሻለ መሆኑን አይተው ሁሉም በአንድ ሐሳብ ሊሾሙት ተስማሙ፤ በአስቄጥስ የሚኖሩ ብዙ ቅዱሳን መነኰሳት ስለ ጽድቁና ስለ ተጋድሎው መስክረውለት ነበርና።

ያለ ፈቃዱ ይዘው አሰሩት። መቃርስም «ወደ ሊቀ ጳጳሳትነት ክብር ልወጣ አይገባኝም፤ እናቴ ሁለት ባሎችን አግብታ ነበርና» እያለ ጮኸ። ይህን ያለው እንዲለቁት ብሎ ነበር እንጂ፣ እናቱ በአንድ ባል ብቻ እንደኖረችና ንጹሕ ሕይወት እንደነበራት ብዙዎች መስክረው ነበር። ስለዚህ ምክንያቱን አልተቀበሉትም። ወደ እስክንድርያ ወስደው ሊቀ ጳጳሳት አድርገው ሾሙት፤ ከዚያም ወደ ምስር (ካይሮ) አመጡት፤ በመዓልቃ በሚገኘው የእመቤታችን የቅድስት ድንግል ማርያም ቤተ ክርስቲያንም የሹመቱ ደብዳቤ በግሪክ፣ በቅብጥና በዐረብኛ ቋንቋ ተነበበ።

በሹመቱ ዘመን ሁሉ መልካም ሥራውን ዕለት ዕለት እየጨመረ በሙሉ ኀይሉ ተጋደለ። በየቀኑ ሕዝቡን እግዚአብሔርን እንዲፈሩ ያስተምራቸውና ይመክራቸው ነበር። ለድሆችና ለችግረኞች ምጽዋት ይሰጥ፣ ምሕረትም ያደርግ ነበር። ከቤተ ክርስቲያን ገንዘብ ምንም አልወሰደም፤ ይልቁንም ከሚደርሰው ገቢ ከፊሉን ለቤተ ክርስቲያንና ለችግረኞች ይሰጥ ነበር። ሃያ ሰባት ዓመት ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ሆኖ ኖረ፤ እግዚአብሔርንም አገልግሎ ደስ አሰኘው፤ በሰላምም አረፈ።
የሙሴ ደቀ መዝሙር የነበረውን የነዌን ልጅ ኢያሱንም እናስባለን።
በአንጾኪያ በሰማዕትነት ያረፉትን ሁለት መቶ ሰዎችም እናስባለን።
የአባ መቃርስ፣ የነዌ ልጅ የኢያሱና የአንጾኪያ ሰማዕታት ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: Shepherd the flock of God which is among you, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion, but voluntarily, not for dishonest gain, but willingly; not as lording it over those entrusted to you, but making yourselves examples to the flock.

am.verse: በእናንተ ዘንድ ያለውን የእግዚአብሔርን መንጋ ጠብቁ፤ እንደእግዚአብሔር ፈቃድ በውድ እንጂ በግድ ሳይሆን፥ በበጎ ፈቃድ እንጂ መጥፎውን ረብ በመመኘት ሳይሆን ጐብኙት፤ ለመንጋው ምሳሌ ሁኑ እንጂ ማኅበሮቻችሁን በኀይል አትግዙ፤

title.en: Martyrdom of St. Sophia and Her Daughters
title.am: የቅድስት ሶፍያና የልጆቿ ሰማዕትነት

en: St. Sophia and Her Two Daughters, Martyrs
St. Mamas the Martyr
Lebna Dengel, King of Ethiopia
am: ቅድስት ሶፍያና ሁለቱ ልጆቿ ሰማዕታት
ቅዱስ ማማስ ሰማዕት
የኢትዮጵያ ንጉሥ ልብነ ድንግል

en: St. Peter Chief of Apostles
Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus
St. John Chrysostom
St. Philip the Apostle
am: ቅዱስ ጴጥሮስ ሊቀ ሐዋርያት
አቡነ ገብረ መንፈስ ቅዱስ
ቅዱስ ዮሐንስ አፈወርቅ
ቅዱስ ፊልጶስ ሐዋርያ

en: On this day the Church remembers the martyrs St. Sophia and her two daughters, Aksosya and Barnaba, and the martyr St. Mamas. We also remember Lebna Dengel, the righteous King of Ethiopia.

Sophia was at first a pagan, and her parents worshipped idols. But she thought it over and saw that their faith was empty, so she went to the bishop of Manufe and said, “I believe in your living God, so baptize me.” The bishop taught her the faith and the law of the Church, and then he baptized her and her daughters in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. After this, some people of the city accused her before the governor, Claudianus, saying that she had stopped worshipping the gods and become a Christian. He questioned her, and she did not deny Christ, so he had her and her daughters tortured cruelly.

In the middle of the torture Sophia encouraged her daughters: “Be strong, my daughters, and be brave.” They answered, “Mother, do not be afraid for us; we will follow in your footsteps,” and they kissed one another. When the governor saw them kissing, he ordered the mother to be whipped, so that her virgin daughters would be frightened. As the cruel men stripped her to beat her, her daughters saw an angel of God come down from heaven and shield their mother. All the while she cried out, “I am a Christian, and I believe in the true God who created the whole world!” The governor ordered her tongue cut out at the root, yet she did not stop crying out and speaking.

Then the governor had her taken to prison and ordered her beheaded with the sword, and she received the crown of victory. A woman secretly took her body to her own house and set a lamp before it. The governor next summoned her daughters and threatened them, and when they refused to obey, he had them beheaded one after the other. So they completed their witness and their struggle. Many wonders appeared at their graves, healing every sickness and disease. When the good King Constantine heard their story, he moved the bodies of the holy martyrs to Constantinople.

Before he heard of Sophia and her daughters, Constantine had ordered a great and spacious house to be built, with an inscription saying, “This is the house of King Constantine.” But each evening, after the workmen had written it, an angel of God came down, wiped it out and wrote, “This is the house of Sophia.” The builders did not know what to do, and they stopped writing.

One day the king's son was playing by himself when an angel appeared to him and asked, “What is the name of this house?” “I do not know,” said the boy. The angel said, “Tell your father to call it the house of Sophia.” The boy asked, “Will you wait for me until I come back?” and the angel answered, “Yes, I will wait for you.” When the king heard this, he knew it was an angel, and he killed his son so that the angel would never leave that place while waiting for the boy. The angel is there to this day, waiting for him. The remains of St. Sophia and her daughters were laid in that church with great praise and honor, and the woman who had gathered their bodies was buried with them.

St. Mamas was still a baby when his parents died in prison, where they had been locked up for their faith in Christ in the days of Emperor Julian. A Christian woman took the child and raised him as her own son. She named him Mamas, which means “orphan,” because he had neither father nor mother. When he was eighteen, people accused him before the governor of being a Christian. They beat him with rods, hung a heavy lead stone around his neck and threw him into the sea, but by the power of God he was saved from drowning. He hid in a cave, where he lived on the milk of wild buffalo.

The governor seized him again and threw him into a blazing fire, but our Lord Jesus Christ saved him. Then lions were let loose on him to tear him apart, but by the power of God Mamas sat on a lion's back. At last they tortured him cruelly and dragged him along until his body was torn apart. In this way Mamas completed his witness and his struggle and received the crown of martyrdom in the kingdom of heaven.
On this day, too, Lebna Dengel, also called Dawit II, the God-loving King of Ethiopia, went to his rest. He held the true faith and was a good and righteous king who reigned from 1508 to 1540 A.D.
May the prayers and blessings of St. Sophia and her daughters, St. Mamas and King Lebna Dengel be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን ሰማዕታቱን ቅድስት ሶፍያንና ሁለቱን ልጆቿን አክሶስናንና በርናባን፣ እንዲሁም ሰማዕቱን ቅዱስ ማማስን ታስባለች። የኢትዮጵያን ጻድቅ ንጉሥ ልብነ ድንግልንም እናስባለን።

ሶፍያ አስቀድማ አረማዊት ነበረች፤ ወላጆቿም ጣዖታትን ያመልኩ ነበር። እርሷ ግን አስባ የእነርሱ ሃይማኖት ከንቱ መሆኑን ተረዳች፤ ወደ መኖፌ ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ሄዳም «በሕያው አምላክህ አምኛለሁና አጥምቀኝ» አለችው። ኤጲስ ቆጶሱም ሃይማኖትንና የቤተ ክርስቲያንን ሕግ አስተማራት፤ ከዚያም እርሷንና ሁለቱን ልጆቿን በአብ፣ በወልድና በመንፈስ ቅዱስ ስም አጠመቃቸው። ከዚህ በኋላ የከተማዋ ሰዎች አማልክትን ማምለክ ትታ ክርስቲያን እንደሆነች በገዢው በከላድያኖስ ፊት ከሰሷት። እርሱም ጠርቶ በጠየቃት ጊዜ ክርስቶስን አልካደችም፤ ስለዚህ እርሷንና ልጆቿን በጽኑ ሥቃይ አሠቃያቸው።

በሥቃዩ መካከል ሶፍያ ልጆቿን ታበረታታቸው ነበር፤ «ልጆቼ ሆይ፣ ጠንክሩ፤ ጨክኑም» አለቻቸው። እነርሱም «እናታችን ሆይ፣ ስለ እኛ አትፍሪ፤ ፈለግሽን እንከተላለን» ብለው መለሱላት፤ እርስ በርሳቸውም ተሳሳሙ። ገዢው ሲሳሳሙ ባየ ጊዜ ደናግል ልጆቿ እንዲፈሩ እናታቸውን በጅራፍ እንዲገርፏት አዘዘ። ጨካኞቹ ሰዎች ሊገርፏት ልብሷን ባወለቁባት ጊዜ ልጆቿ የእግዚአብሔር መልአክ ከሰማይ ወርዶ እናታቸውን ሲጋርዳት አዩ። እርሷም በዚያን ጊዜ ሁሉ «ክርስቲያን ነኝ፤ ዓለሙን ሁሉ በፈጠረ በእውነተኛው አምላክም አምናለሁ!» እያለች ትጮኽ ነበር። ገዢው ምላሷን ከሥሩ እንዲቈርጡ አዘዘ፤ እርሷ ግን መጮኽንና መናገርን አላቆመችም።

ከዚያም ገዢው ወደ ወኅኒ እንዲወስዷት አዘዘ፤ አንገቷንም በሰይፍ አስቈረጠ፤ እርሷም የድል አክሊልን ተቀበለች። አንዲት ሴት ሥጋዋን በስውር ወደ ቤቷ ወስዳ በሥጋዋ ፊት መብራት አኖረች። ገዢው ቀጥሎ ልጆቿን ጠርቶ እንዲታዘዙለት አስፈራራቸው፤ እምቢ ባሉትም ጊዜ አንድ በአንድ አንገታቸውን አስቈረጠ፤ እነርሱም ምስክርነታቸውንና ተጋድሏቸውን ፈጸሙ። ከመቃብራቸውም በሽታንና ደዌን ሁሉ የሚፈውሱ ብዙ ድንቅ ተአምራት ተገለጡ። ደጉ ንጉሥ ቁስጠንጢኖስ ዜናቸውን በሰማ ጊዜ የቅዱሳት ሰማዕታቱን ሥጋ ወደ ቁስጥንጥንያ አፈለሰ።

ቁስጠንጢኖስ የሶፍያንና የልጆቿን ዜና ከመስማቱ በፊት ታላቅና ሰፊ ቤት እንዲሠራ፣ በላዩም «ይህ ቤት የንጉሥ ቁስጠንጢኖስ ነው» የሚል ጽሑፍ እንዲጻፍ አዝዞ ነበር። ሠራተኞቹ ወደ ማታ ይህን በጻፉ ጊዜ ሁሉ የእግዚአብሔር መልአክ ወርዶ ያጠፋውና «ይህ ቤት የሶፍያ ነው» ብሎ ይጽፍ ነበር። ሠሪዎቹም ምን እንደሚያደርጉ አጥተው መጻፋቸውን ተዉ።

አንድ ቀን የንጉሡ ልጅ ብቻውን ሲጫወት መልአክ ተገልጦለት «የዚህ ቤት ስም ማን ነው?» አለው። ሕፃኑም «አላውቅም» አለው። መልአኩም «አባትህ የሶፍያ ቤት ብሎ እንዲጠራው ንገረው» አለው። ሕፃኑም «እስክመለስ ድረስ ትጠብቀኛለህን?» አለው፤ መልአኩም «አዎን፣ እጠብቅሃለሁ» አለው። ንጉሡ ይህን ሰምቶ መልአክ መሆኑን አወቀ፤ መልአኩ ሕፃኑን እየጠበቀ ከዚያ ቦታ እንዳይሄድ ልጁን ገደለው። መልአኩ እስከ ዛሬ ድረስ እየጠበቀው በዚያ አለ። የቅድስት ሶፍያና የልጆቿ ሥጋ በታላቅ ምስጋናና ክብር በዚያች ቤተ ክርስቲያን ተቀመጠ፤ ሥጋቸውን የሰበሰበችው ሴትም ከእነርሱ ጋር ተቀበረች።

ቅዱስ ማማስ ገና ሕፃን ሳለ ወላጆቹ በንጉሥ ዑልያኖስ ዘመን ስለ ክርስቶስ ሃይማኖት ታስረው በወኅኒ ውስጥ አረፉ። አንዲት ክርስቲያን ሴት ሕፃኑን ወስዳ እንደ ልጇ አሳደገችው፤ አባትም እናትም ስላልነበሩት «ማማስ» የሚል ስም አወጣችለት፤ ትርጉሙም «የሙት ልጅ» ነው። ዕድሜው ዐሥራ ስምንት ዓመት ሲሆን ሰዎች ክርስቲያን መሆኑን በገዢው ፊት ከሰሱት። በበትር ደበደቡት፤ በአንገቱም ከባድ የእርሳስ ድንጋይ አንጠልጥለው ወደ ባሕር ጣሉት፤ እርሱ ግን በእግዚአብሔር ኀይል ከመስመጥ ዳነ። ወጥቶም በዋሻ ውስጥ ተሠውሮ የጎሽ ወተት እየጠጣ ኖረ።

ገዢው ዳግመኛ ይዞ በሚነድ እሳት ውስጥ ጨመረው፤ ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ ግን አዳነው። ከዚያም ተነጣጥቀው እንዲበሉት አንበሶችን በላዩ ለቀቁበት፤ ማማስ ግን በእግዚአብሔር ኀይል በአንበሳ ጀርባ ላይ ተቀመጠ። በመጨረሻም ብዙ አሠቃዩት፤ ሰውነቱ እስኪበጣጠስ ድረስም ጎተቱት። በዚህም ምስክርነቱንና ተጋድሎውን ፈጸመ፤ በመንግሥተ ሰማያትም የሰማዕትነትን አክሊል ተቀበለ።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ እግዚአብሔርን የሚወደው የኢትዮጵያ ንጉሥ ልብነ ድንግል፣ ዳግማዊ ዳዊትም ተብሎ የሚጠራው፣ አረፈ። በቀናች ሃይማኖት የጸና ደግና ጻድቅ ንጉሥ ነበር፤ ከ1508 እስከ 1540 እ.ኤ.አ. ነገሠ።
የቅድስት ሶፍያና የልጆቿ፣ የቅዱስ ማማስና የንጉሥ ልብነ ድንግል ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven.

am.verse: ስለዚህ፥ በሰው ፊት ለሚመሰክርልኝ ሁሉ፥ እኔ ደግሞ በሰማያት ባለው በአባቴ ፊት እመሰክርለታለሁ፤

title.en: Martyrdom of the Prophet Isaiah
title.am: የነቢዩ ኢሳይያስ ሰማዕትነት

en: Isaiah the Prophet
St. Baslantya the Martyr
Saints James, Anatimos, Baslis, Arontos, Wurwa, Sawlis and Sewlas
am: ነቢዩ ኢሳይያስ
ቅድስት ሰብልትንያ ሰማዕት
ቅዱሳን ያዕቆብ፣ አናቲሞስ፣ ባስሊስ፣ አሮንጦስ፣ ውርዋ፣ ሳውልስና ሰውላስ

en: Holy Mount Qusqwam
St. Arsema the Virgin Martyr
St. Basil of Caesarea
St. Marina
am: ቅድስት ደብረ ቁስቋም
ቅድስት አርሴማ ድንግል
ቅዱስ ባስልዮስ ዘቂሣርያ
ቅድስት መሪና

en: On this day the Church remembers the great prophet Isaiah, who was martyred under King Manasseh. We also remember the child martyr St. Baslantya, and James the monk, Bishop Anatimos, Baslis, Arontos, Wurwa, Sawlis and Sewlas, the martyrs of God.

Isaiah, the son of Amoz, prophesied in the days of five kings of Judah: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah and Manasseh. To King Ahaz he spoke of the sign God would give: “A virgin will conceive and bear a son, and his name will be called Immanuel,” which means “God with us.” He said that this child would save his people from the punishment their sins deserved and bring the nations into his faith. He would put an end to the old sacrifices and priesthood of Israel and appoint new priests to offer him praise.

When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem and blasphemed against God, Isaiah told King Hezekiah that God would destroy him. That same night God sent the archangel Michael to the enemy camp, and he struck down 185,000 soldiers. Later Hezekiah fell sick and was close to death, and God told him through Isaiah to put his house in order, because he was going to die. Hezekiah turned his face to the wall, prayed and wept bitterly. Then God sent Isaiah back to tell him that he had heard his prayer, seen his tears and added fifteen years to his life, and he gave him a sign so that he could be sure the prophet's words were true.

Isaiah also prophesied that the people of Israel would be taken captive and later brought back from their captivity. He foretold the sufferings of our Lord Jesus Christ, who would be led like a lamb to the slaughter and, like a sheep before its shearers, would not open his mouth in his suffering. God worked wonders through the prophet as well: he made a spring of water flow, and at Isaiah's prayer he sent rain once the people had obeyed.

Isaiah also prophesied to King Manasseh, the son of Hezekiah, who had set up idols and worshiped them, and he rebuked the king for his evil deeds. Manasseh was furious and sawed him in two with a wood saw, from his head to his feet, and in this way Isaiah finished his testimony. His time as a prophet lasted seventy years and more, and he prophesied 913 years before the coming of Christ our Lord.

On this day, too, the holy woman Baslantya died as a martyr in the days of Diocletian, the emperor who denied Christ. She was a Christian, and when she was only nine years old, those who had denied the Lord seized her, bound her hands and feet and threw her into a fire, but the power of God saved her from the flames. When she grew thirsty she asked God for water, and he caused water to flow for her, so she drank and praised the Lord. Then she committed her soul into the hands of God and cast herself into the fire, and so she completed her testimony.
We also remember James the monk, Bishop Anatimos, Baslis, Arontos, Wurwa, Sawlis and Sewlas, the martyrs of God.
May the prayers and blessings of the prophet Isaiah, St. Baslantya and the other saints of this day be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን በንጉሥ ምናሴ ዘመን በሰማዕትነት ያረፈውን ታላቁን ነቢይ ኢሳይያስን ታስባለች። ሕፃኗን ሰማዕት ቅድስት ሰብልትንያን፣ እንዲሁም የእግዚአብሔር ሰማዕታት የሆኑትን መነኰሱን ያዕቆብን፣ ኤጲስ ቆጶሱን አናቲሞስን፣ ባስሊስን፣ አሮንጦስን፣ ውርዋን፣ ሳውልስንና ሰውላስንም እናስባለን።

የአሞጽ ልጅ ኢሳይያስ ትንቢት የተናገረው በአምስት የይሁዳ ነገሥታት ማለትም በአዝያን፣ በኢዮአታም፣ በአካዝ፣ በሕዝቅያስና በምናሴ ዘመን ነው። ለንጉሥ አካዝ እግዚአብሔር የሚሰጠውን ምልክት ተናገረ፦ «ድንግል ትጸንሳለች፤ ወንድ ልጅም ትወልዳለች፤ ስሙም አማኑኤል ይባላል»፤ ትርጓሜውም «እግዚአብሔር ከእኛ ጋር» የሚል ነው። ይህ ልጅ ወገኖቹን ኃጢአታቸው ከሚያስከትልባቸው ቅጣት እንደሚያድናቸው፣ አሕዛብንም ወደ ሃይማኖቱ እንደሚያስገባ ተናገረ። ደግሞም የእስራኤልን የቀድሞ መሥዋዕትና ክህነት እንደሚያስቀርና እርሱን የሚያመሰግኑ አዲስ ካህናትን እንደሚሾም ተናገረ።

ንጉሥ ሰናክሬም ኢየሩሳሌምን ከብቦ እግዚአብሔርን በተሳደበ ጊዜ ኢሳይያስ እግዚአብሔር እንደሚያጠፋው ለንጉሥ ሕዝቅያስ ነገረው። በዚያችው ሌሊት እግዚአብሔር ሊቀ መላእክት ቅዱስ ሚካኤልን ወደ ጠላት ሰፈር ላከ፤ እርሱም 185,000 ወታደሮችን ገደለ። በኋላም ሕዝቅያስ ታሞ ለሞት ተቃረበ፤ እግዚአብሔርም ሊሞት ስለሆነ ቤቱን እንዲያዘጋጅ በኢሳይያስ አማካኝነት ነገረው። ሕዝቅያስ ፊቱን ወደ ግድግዳ መልሶ ጸለየ፤ ምርር ብሎም አለቀሰ። ከዚያም እግዚአብሔር ኢሳይያስን መልሶ ላከው፤ ጸሎቱን እንደሰማ፣ ዕንባውንም እንዳየና በዕድሜው ላይ ዐሥራ አምስት ዓመት እንደጨመረለት እንዲነግረው አዘዘው፤ ነቢዩ የተናገረው እውነት መሆኑን እንዲያውቅም ምልክት ሰጠው።

ኢሳይያስ የእስራኤል ሕዝብ በምርኮ እንደሚወሰድና ከምርኮውም እንደሚመለስ ትንቢት ተናገረ። ስለ ጌታችን ስለ ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ መከራም አስቀድሞ ተናገረ፤ እርሱ እንደ በግ ለመታረድ እንደሚነዳና በሸላቾቹ ፊት ዝም እንደሚል በግ በመከራው ጊዜ አፉን እንደማይከፍት ተናገረ። እግዚአብሔር በነቢዩ እጅ ተአምራትንም አደረገ፤ የውኃ ምንጭ አፈለቀ፤ ሕዝቡም በታዘዙ ጊዜ በኢሳይያስ ጸሎት ዝናብ አዘነበ።

ኢሳይያስ የሕዝቅያስ ልጅ ለሆነው ለንጉሥ ምናሴም ትንቢት ተናገረ፤ ምናሴ ጣዖታትን አቁሞ ያመልክ ስለነበር ስለ ክፉ ሥራው ገሠጸው። ምናሴ እጅግ ተቈጥቶ ነቢዩን በዕንጨት መጋዝ ከራሱ እስከ እግሩ ለሁለት ሰነጠቀው፤ ኢሳይያስም በዚህ ምስክርነቱን ፈጸመ። ነቢይ ሆኖ የኖረበት ዘመን ከሰባ ዓመት በላይ ነበር፤ ትንቢት የተናገረውም ጌታችን ክርስቶስ ከመምጣቱ 913 ዓመት በፊት ነበር።

በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ክርስቶስን በካደው ንጉሥ በዲዮቅልጥያኖስ ዘመን ቅድስት ሰብልትንያ በሰማዕትነት አረፈች። ክርስቲያን ነበረች፤ ገና የዘጠኝ ዓመት ልጅ ሳለች ጌታን የካዱ ሰዎች ይዘው እጅና እግሯን አስረው ወደ እሳት ጣሏት፤ የእግዚአብሔር ኃይል ግን ከእሳቱ አዳናት። በተጠማች ጊዜ እግዚአብሔርን ውኃ ለመነችው፤ እርሱም ውኃ አፈለቀላት፤ እርሷም ጠጥታ ጌታን አመሰገነች። ከዚያም ነፍሷን ለእግዚአብሔር አደራ ሰጥታ ወደ እሳቱ ራሷን ጣለች፤ በዚህም ምስክርነቷን ፈጸመች።
የእግዚአብሔር ሰማዕታት የሆኑትን መነኰሱን ያዕቆብን፣ ኤጲስ ቆጶሱን አናቲሞስን፣ ባስሊስን፣ አሮንጦስን፣ ውርዋን፣ ሳውልስንና ሰውላስንም እናስባለን።
የነቢዩ የኢሳይያስ፣ የቅድስት ሰብልትንያና የዚህች ዕለት ሌሎች ቅዱሳን ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: “Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel;” which is, being interpreted, “God with us.”

am.verse: እንሆ፥ ድንግል ትፀንሳለች ልጅም ትወልዳለች፥ ስሙንም ዐማኑኤል ይሉታል የተባለው ይፈጸም ዘንድ ይህ ሁሉ ሆኗል፥ ትርጓሜውም፦ እግዚአብሔር ከእኛ ጋራ የሚል ነው።

title.en: Abba Dioscorus, Archbishop of Alexandria
title.am: አባ ዲዮስቆሮስ የእስክንድርያ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት

en: Abba Dioscorus, Archbishop of Alexandria
Abba Severianus, Bishop of Gabla
Saints Agathon, Peter, John and Ammon, with Their Mother Rebecca, Martyrs
St. Fasilides and His Companions, Martyrs
Das of Gangra, Bishop Nawla of Antioch, and Peter the Monk
The Birth of St. Hanna, Mother of Our Lady
Elizabeth, Mother of John the Baptist
am: አባ ዲዮስቆሮስ የእስክንድርያ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት
አባ ሳዊርያኖስ የገብላ ኤጲስ ቆጶስ
ቅዱሳን አጋቶን፣ ጴጥሮስ፣ ዮሐንስና አሞን ከእናታቸው ከራፈቃ ጋር ሰማዕታት
ቅዱስ ፋሲለደስና ባልንጀሮቹ ሰማዕታት
የጋንግራው ዳስ፣ የአንጾኪያው ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ናውላና መነኰሴው ጴጥሮስ
የእመቤታችን እናት የቅድስት ሐና ልደት
የመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ እናት ኤልሳቤጥ

en: The Holy Trinity
Abba Giyorgis of Gascha
Abba Sinoda of Denderah
St. Athanasius the Apostolic
am: ቅድስት ሥላሴ
አባ ጊዮርጊስ ዘጋስጫ
አባ ሲኖዳ ዘደንድራ
ቅዱስ አትናቴዎስ ሐዋርያዊ

en: On this day the Church remembers Abba Dioscorus, Archbishop of Alexandria, and Abba Severianus, Bishop of Gabla. We also remember the martyrs Agathon, Peter, John and Ammon with their mother Rebecca; St. Fasilides and his companions; Das of Gangra, Bishop Nawla of Antioch and Peter the monk; the birth of St. Hanna, the mother of Our Lady; and the repose of Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist.

Dioscorus, the twenty-fifth Archbishop of Alexandria, was summoned by Emperor Marcian to a great council of more than six hundred bishops. He asked what was lacking in the faith that so large an assembly was needed, and when they told him the emperor had called it, he said, “If our Lord Jesus Christ called this council, I will stay and speak what God gives me. If the emperor called it, let him run it himself.” Then he tore up the letter of Leo, Archbishop of Rome, which taught that after the union Christ has two natures and two wills.

Speaking by the Holy Spirit, Dioscorus taught that Christ is one: the same Lord who was invited to the wedding at Cana as a man turned the water into wine as God. As Abba Cyril had said, the Word of God is united with the flesh like the soul with the body and like fire with iron. Some of the bishops told the emperor and the empress that only Dioscorus opposed their commands about the faith. Since he would not change his belief, the angry emperor and empress had him beaten, his beard plucked out and his teeth broken. Dioscorus sent the hair and the teeth to Alexandria, saying, “This is the fruit of the Orthodox faith.”

Frightened, the other bishops signed the emperor's paper, which declared that Christ has two natures. When Dioscorus asked for it, they sent it, expecting him to sign too. Instead he wrote at the bottom and excommunicated them all, and everyone who departs from the faith of the apostles and the 318 fathers of Nicea. The furious emperor banished him to the island of Gagra. The Nestorian bishop there treated him with contempt, until God worked wonders through his hands and all the people honored him. Having finished his good fight, Dioscorus received the crown of faith, entered eternal rest and was buried on the island.

Severianus studied in Athens, Caesarea and Rome, and knew the Old and New Testaments by heart. When his parents died, he gave all the wealth they left him to Christ and built a house for travelers, the poor and the afflicted. When he was accused before Emperor Honorius of giving it all away, the emperor loved him for it and kept him close. Afraid that his labor would be lost in empty praise, Severianus left secretly by night at the command of an angel to become the father of the monastery of Gabla. A light like a wheel went before him on the way.

At Gabla God worked wonders through the saint's hands: when Satan possessed the governor's daughter, a note from Severianus, “In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, come out of her,” drove him out at once. Made Bishop of Gabla, he led a learned Jew named Sektor and many others to baptism, and Satan groaned, “Severianus has taken from me the one place I had left.” He rebuked Empress Eudoxia for banishing John Chrysostom, and his discourses are still read in Orthodox churches. He lived a hundred years, and after charging his people to keep God's law, he died in peace.

Agathon, Peter, John and Ammon were brothers from Upper Egypt, and their mother was Rebecca. Christ appeared to them and told them that they would receive the crown of martyrdom in the city of Sebra, near Alexandria. They rose early and gave all their possessions to the poor, and Rebecca urged them to endure suffering for the name of Christ. They confessed their faith in Christ before the governor Dionysius, who tortured their mother first, and she bore it bravely and with joy. Then he tortured her four sons and finally sent them on to Alexandria.

At Sebra, Armenius, the governor of Alexandria, cut their flesh with knives, put them on the wheel and hung them upside down, but each time Christ raised them up unharmed, until the governor and his men were ashamed. He then had them beheaded and their bodies put in a small boat to be thrown into the sea. But God sent an angel to a rich man of Nekraha, who took the holy bodies and heard a voice say, “This is the dwelling of the righteous.” When the persecution had passed, a fine church was built for them, where God worked great wonders through their bones.
On this day, too, St. Fasilides died as a martyr together with two thousand of his companions.
We also remember Das of Gangra, Bishop Nawla of Antioch, and Peter the monk.
The Church also remembers the birth of St. Hanna, the mother of Our Lady the Virgin Mary.
On this day, too, Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist, went to her rest.
May the prayers and blessings of Abba Dioscorus, Abba Severianus, Saints Agathon, Peter, John and Ammon, their mother Rebecca, St. Fasilides and all the saints of this day be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን የእስክንድርያውን ሊቀ ጳጳሳት አባ ዲዮስቆሮስንና የገብላውን ኤጲስ ቆጶስ አባ ሳዊርያኖስን ታስባለች። ሰማዕታቱን አጋቶንን፣ ጴጥሮስን፣ ዮሐንስንና አሞንን ከእናታቸው ከራፈቃ ጋር፤ ቅዱስ ፋሲለደስንና ባልንጀሮቹን፤ የጋንግራውን ዳስን፣ የአንጾኪያውን ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ናውላንና መነኰሴውን ጴጥሮስንም፤ እንዲሁም የእመቤታችን እናት ቅድስት ሐና የተወለደችበትንና የመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ እናት ኤልሳቤጥ ያረፈችበትን ቀን እናስባለን።

ሃያ አምስተኛው የእስክንድርያ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ዲዮስቆሮስ ከስድስት መቶ በላይ ኤጲስ ቆጶሳት ወደ ተሰበሰቡበት ታላቅ ጉባኤ በንጉሥ መርቅያኖስ ተጠራ። በሃይማኖት ላይ ምን ጎድሎ ነው እንዲህ ያለ ታላቅ ጉባኤ የሚያስፈልገው ብሎ ጠየቀ፤ ንጉሡ እንደ ጠራው በነገሩት ጊዜም እንዲህ አለ፦ «ይህን ጉባኤ የጠራው ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ ከሆነ እኔ እቆያለሁ፤ እግዚአብሔርም የሚሰጠኝን እናገራለሁ። ንጉሡ የጠራው ከሆነ ግን ጉባኤውን ራሱ ይምራው።» ከዚያም የሮሜው ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ልዮን የጻፈውን ደብዳቤ ቀደደ፤ ደብዳቤው ከተዋሕዶ በኋላ ክርስቶስ ሁለት ባሕርይና ሁለት ፈቃድ አለው ብሎ ያስተምር ነበር።

በመንፈስ ቅዱስ እየተናገረ ዲዮስቆሮስ ክርስቶስ አንድ እንደሆነ አስተማረ፤ እንደ ሰው ወደ ቃና ሠርግ የተጠራው ጌታ ራሱ እንደ አምላክ ውኃውን ወይን አደረገው። አባ ቄርሎስ እንዳስተማረው የእግዚአብሔር ቃል ከሥጋ ጋር መዋሐዱ ነፍስ ከሥጋ ጋር፣ እሳትም ከብረት ጋር እንደሚዋሐድ ያለ ነው። ከኤጲስ ቆጶሳቱ አንዳንዶቹ በሃይማኖት ጉዳይ ትእዛዛቸውን የሚቃወም ከዲዮስቆሮስ በቀር ማንም እንደሌለ ለንጉሡና ለንግሥቲቱ ነገሯቸው። እምነቱንም ስላልለወጠ ንጉሡና ንግሥቲቱ ተቆጥተው እንዲደበድቡት አዘዙ፤ ጢሙ ተነጨ፤ ጥርሶቹም ተሰበሩ። ዲዮስቆሮስ የተነጨውን ጢሙንና የተሰበሩትን ጥርሶቹን ወደ እስክንድርያ ልኮ «ይህ የቀናች ሃይማኖት ፍሬ ነው» አለ።

ሌሎቹ ኤጲስ ቆጶሳት ፈርተው ክርስቶስ ሁለት ባሕርይ እንዳለው በሚናገረው በንጉሡ ወረቀት ላይ ፈረሙ። ዲዮስቆሮስ ያንን ወረቀት በጠየቀ ጊዜ እርሱም እንደ እነርሱ እንደሚፈርምበት ስላሰቡ ላኩለት። እርሱ ግን በወረቀቱ ግርጌ ጽፎ ሁሉንም አወገዛቸው፤ ከሐዋርያትና በኒቅያ ከተሰበሰቡት ከ318 አባቶች እምነት የሚለየውንም ሁሉ አወገዘ። የተቆጣው ንጉሥ ወደ ጋግራ ደሴት አሰደደው። የዚያ አገር ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ንስጥሮሳዊ ስለ ሆነ ዲዮስቆሮስን ናቀው፤ ነገር ግን እግዚአብሔር በዲዮስቆሮስ እጅ ተአምራትን ባደረገ ጊዜ የደሴቲቱ ሰዎች ሁሉ አከበሩት። መልካሙን ገድል ከተጋደለ በኋላ የሃይማኖትን አክሊል ተቀብሎ ወደ ዘላለም ዕረፍት ገባ፤ በዚያችው ደሴትም ተቀበረ።

ሳዊርያኖስ በአቴና፣ በቂሣርያና በሮሜ ተምሮ የብሉይንና የሐዲስን መጻሕፍት በቃሉ ያውቅ ነበር። ወላጆቹ ሲሞቱ የተዉለትን ሀብት ሁሉ ለክርስቶስ ሰጠ፤ መንገደኞችን፣ ድሆችንና ችግረኞችን የሚቀበል ቤትም ሠራ። ሀብቱን ሁሉ በመስጠቱ በንጉሥ አኖሬዎስ ፊት በተከሰሰ ጊዜ ንጉሡ በዚህ የተነሣ ወደደው፤ ከእርሱም አላራቀውም። ድካሙ በከንቱ ውዳሴ እንዳይጠፋ ፈርቶ መልአክ እንዳዘዘው በሌሊት በስውር ወጣ፤ የገብላ ገዳም አባት ለመሆን ሄደ። እንደ መንኰራኵር ያለ ብርሃንም በፊቱ እየሄደ ይመራው ነበር።

በገብላ እግዚአብሔር በቅዱሱ እጅ ድንቅ ተአምራትን አደረገ፤ ሰይጣን በአገረ ገዥው ልጅ ላይ ባደረ ጊዜ ሳዊርያኖስ የጻፈው «በጌታችን በኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ ስም ከእርሷ ውጣ» የሚል ወረቀት ሰይጣንን ወዲያውኑ አስወጣው። የገብላ ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ከሆነ በኋላ ስቅጣር የተባለ አዋቂ አይሁዳዊንና ሌሎች ብዙ ሰዎችን ወደ ጥምቀት መራ፤ ሰይጣንም «ለእኔ የቀረችኝን አንዲቷን ስፍራ ሳዊርያኖስ ነጠቀኝ» ብሎ ቃተተ። ዮሐንስ አፈወርቅን ስላሰደደች ንግሥት አውዶክስያን ገሠጻት፤ የጻፋቸው ድርሳናትም እስከ ዛሬ በቀናች ሃይማኖት በሚመሩ አብያተ ክርስቲያናት ይነበባሉ። መቶ ዓመት ኖረ፤ ሕዝቡንም የእግዚአብሔርን ሕግ እንዲጠብቁ ካዘዛቸው በኋላ በሰላም አረፈ።

አጋቶን፣ ጴጥሮስ፣ ዮሐንስና አሞን ከላይኛው ግብፅ የመጡ ወንድማማቾች ነበሩ፤ እናታቸውም ራፈቃ ትባላለች። ጌታችን ክርስቶስ ተገልጦላቸው በእስክንድርያ አቅራቢያ በምትገኘው በስብራ ከተማ የሰማዕትነትን አክሊል እንደሚቀበሉ ነገራቸው። በማለዳ ተነሥተው ያላቸውን ሁሉ ለድሆች ሰጡ፤ ራፈቃም ስለ ክርስቶስ ስም መከራን እንዲታገሡ አበረታታቻቸው። በገዥው በዲዮናሲዮስ ፊት በክርስቶስ ማመናቸውን መሰከሩ፤ እርሱም እናታቸውን አስቀድሞ አሠቃያት፤ እርሷም በጀግንነትና በደስታ ታገሠች። ከዚያም አራቱን ልጆቿን አሠቃያቸው፤ በመጨረሻም ወደ እስክንድርያ ላካቸው።

በስብራ የእስክንድርያ አገረ ገዥ አርማንዮስ ሥጋቸውን በቢላዋ ቆራረጠ፣ በመንኰራኵር ላይ ጣላቸው፣ ዘቅዝቆም ሰቀላቸው፤ ነገር ግን ክርስቶስ ገዥውና ሰዎቹ እስኪያፍሩ ድረስ ደጋግሞ ያለ ጉዳት ያነሣቸው ነበር። ከዚያም ራሳቸውን በሰይፍ አስቆረጠ፤ ሥጋቸውንም ወደ ባሕር ለመጣል በትንሽ ታንኳ ላይ ጫኑ። እግዚአብሔር ግን በነቅራሃ ወደሚኖር አንድ ሀብታም ሰው መልአኩን ላከ፤ እርሱም የቅዱሳኑን ሥጋ ወስዶ «ይህ የጻድቃን ማደሪያ ነው» የሚል ድምፅ ሰማ። ስደቱ ካለፈ በኋላ ያማረች ቤተ ክርስቲያን ተሠራላቸው፤ እግዚአብሔርም በዚያ ከአጥንቶቻቸው ታላላቅ ተአምራትን አደረገ።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ቅዱስ ፋሲለደስ ከሁለት ሺህ ባልንጀሮቹ ጋር በሰማዕትነት አረፈ።
የጋንግራውን ዳስን፣ የአንጾኪያውን ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ናውላንና መነኰሴውን ጴጥሮስንም እናስባለን።
ቤተ ክርስቲያን የእመቤታችን የቅድስት ድንግል ማርያም እናት የቅድስት ሐናን ልደትም ታስባለች።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ የመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ እናት ኤልሳቤጥ አረፈች።
የአባ ዲዮስቆሮስ፣ የአባ ሳዊርያኖስ፣ የቅዱሳን አጋቶን፣ ጴጥሮስ፣ ዮሐንስና አሞን፣ የእናታቸው የራፈቃ፣ የቅዱስ ፋሲለደስና የዚህች ዕለት የቅዱሳን ሁሉ ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.

am.verse: መልካሙን ገድል ተጋድያለሁ፥ ሩጫውን ጨርሻለሁ፥ ሃይማኖትን ጠብቄያለሁ፤

title.en: St. Zacharias the Priest and Moses the Prophet
title.am: ቅዱስ ዘካርያስ ካህን እና ነቢዩ ሙሴ

en: St. Zacharias the Priest, Father of John the Baptist
Moses, Chief of the Prophets
St. Dimasius the Martyr
St. Lucius the Martyr
Saints Jeremiah and Elianos, and Ammon the Monk
St. Cyriacus the Desert Father
am: ቅዱስ ዘካርያስ ካህን የመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ አባት
ሙሴ ሊቀ ነቢያት
ቅዱስ ዲማድዮስ ሰማዕት
ቅዱስ ሉክዮስ ሰማዕት
ቅዱሳን ኤርምያስና ኤልያኖስ፣ እንዲሁም መነኰስ አሞን
ቅዱስ ቂርቆስ ገዳማዊ

en: The Four Living Creatures (Cherubim)
Abba Kiros the Righteous
Moses the Prophet
Abba John Kama
am: አርባዕቱ እንስሳ (ኪሩቤል)
አባ ኪሮስ ጻድቅ
ሙሴ ሊቀ ነቢያት
አባ ዮሐንስ ካማ

en: On this day the Church remembers the martyrdom of St. Zacharias the priest, the father of John the Baptist, and the repose of Moses, the chief of the prophets. We also remember the martyrs St. Dimasius and St. Lucius, Saints Jeremiah and Elianos, the monk Ammon, and the desert father St. Cyriacus.

Zacharias, the son of Berechiah, was a priest, and the Gospel bears witness that he and his wife were righteous and walked blamelessly in the Law of God. When the archangel Gabriel announced the birth of John, Zacharias did not believe him and was struck mute until the child was born. Then his tongue was loosed, and he praised God and wrote, “His name is John.”

When Christ was born, King Herod grew afraid for his kingdom and had all the children of Bethlehem who were two years old or younger put to death. John's mother, Elizabeth, fled with her child into the wilderness of Sinai and raised him there for seven years. After she died, the boy lived alone in the desert until the day he would show himself to Israel.

Later Herod suspected that John was the Christ and sent soldiers to Zacharias to find the child. Zacharias said he did not know where the boy or his mother was, and he was not afraid when Herod threatened to kill him. So Herod's soldiers killed him between the sanctuary and the altar. God hid his body, and his blood turned hard like stone. When the priests came to pray as usual, one of them went into the sanctuary, found the blood, and heard a voice from the altar crying out, “Zacharias, the son of Berechiah, has been slain!” His blood kept crying out until it was avenged, which is why our Lord told the Jews, “The blood of Zacharias, whom you killed, will come upon you.”

On this day, too, Moses, the righteous chief of the prophets, died. Pharaoh had ordered every Hebrew boy to be destroyed, so his parents cast Moses into the river, but Pharaoh's daughter found him and raised him as her own son. At forty he killed an Egyptian who was attacking a Hebrew and fled to Midian, and at eighty God spoke to him from a burning bush and sent him to bring the Israelites out of Egypt. Through Moses God struck Egypt with ten plagues, parted the Red Sea for Israel and drowned Pharaoh and his army in it, and for forty years in the wilderness fed his people with manna and gave them water from a rock.

Though the people often cursed Moses and wanted to stone him, he loved them so much that he prayed, “If you will not forgive this people their sin, blot my name out of your book.” God spoke with him as a man speaks with a friend, and his face shone with God's glory. When Moses was a hundred and twenty years old, he handed the people over to his disciple Joshua, son of Nun, and died on the mountain. God hid his body so that the Israelites would not take it and worship it, and when Satan tried to reveal it, the archangel Michael rebuked him, as the apostle Jude testifies.

On this day, too, St. Dimasius, a native of the city of Derseba, died as a martyr. He loved the Church and the poor and visited the sick, and when a man shining with light told him to go and receive the crown of martyrdom, he left his father and mother and his city. In Athribis he confessed Christ before the governor, who tortured him cruelly and sent him on to Lucianus, the governor of Alexandria. On the boat our Lord Jesus Christ appeared to him and promised him everlasting joy. Lucianus tortured him and had him beheaded with the sword, and he received the crown of martyrdom in the kingdom of heaven. His townspeople took his body and honored it, and mighty wonders took place through it.
The martyr St. Lucius is also remembered today. A governor tortured him again and again and finally had him beheaded with the sword, and he received the crown of martyrdom.
Saints Jeremiah and Elianos, and Ammon the monk, are remembered on this day as well.
On this day, too, the holy desert father St. Cyriacus went to his rest. His food was the milk of a deer, and many miracles took place when he died.
May the prayers and blessings of St. Zacharias, Moses the prophet, St. Dimasius, St. Lucius, Saints Jeremiah and Elianos, Ammon and St. Cyriacus be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን የመጥምቁ ዮሐንስ አባት የካህኑ የቅዱስ ዘካርያስን ሰማዕትነትና የነቢያት አለቃ የሙሴን ዕረፍት ታስባለች። ሰማዕታቱን ቅዱስ ዲማድዮስንና ቅዱስ ሉክዮስን፣ ቅዱሳን ኤርምያስንና ኤልያኖስን፣ መነኰሱን አሞንንና ገዳማዊውን ቅዱስ ቂርቆስንም እናስባለን።

የበራክዩ ልጅ ዘካርያስ ካህን ነበር፤ እርሱና ሚስቱ ጻድቃን እንደ ነበሩና በእግዚአብሔር ሕግ ያለ ነቀፋ እንደ ኖሩ ወንጌል ይመሰክራል። ሊቀ መላእክት ገብርኤል የዮሐንስን መወለድ በነገረው ጊዜ ዘካርያስ ስላላመነ ሕፃኑ እስኪወለድ ድረስ ዲዳ ሆነ። ከዚያም አንደበቱ ተፈታ፤ እግዚአብሔርንም አመሰገነ፤ «ስሙ ዮሐንስ ነው» ብሎም ጻፈ።

ክርስቶስ በተወለደ ጊዜ ንጉሥ ሄሮድስ ለመንግሥቱ ፈርቶ ሁለት ዓመት የሆናቸውንና ከዚያ በታች የሆኑትን የቤተ ልሔም ሕፃናት ሁሉ አስገደለ። የዮሐንስ እናት ኤልሳቤጥ ደግሞ ልጇን ይዛ ወደ ሲና በረሃ ሸሸች፤ በዚያም ሰባት ዓመት አሳደገችው። እርሷ ካረፈች በኋላ ሕፃኑ ራሱን ለእስራኤል እስኪገልጥ ድረስ በበረሃ ብቻውን ኖረ።

ከዚያ በኋላ ሄሮድስ ዮሐንስ ክርስቶስ ይሆናል ብሎ ጠረጠረ፤ ሕፃኑን እንዲፈልጉም ወታደሮችን ወደ ዘካርያስ ላከ። ዘካርያስም ሕፃኑና እናቱ የት እንዳሉ እንደማያውቅ ነገራቸው፤ ሄሮድስ እንደሚገድለው ባስፈራራው ጊዜም አልፈራም። ስለዚህ የሄሮድስ ወታደሮች በመቅደሱና በመሠዊያው መካከል ገደሉት። እግዚአብሔር ሥጋውን ሠወረ፤ ደሙም እንደ ድንጋይ ደነደነ። ካህናቱ እንደ ልማዳቸው ሊጸልዩ በመጡ ጊዜ ከእነርሱ አንዱ ወደ መቅደሱ ገባ፤ ደሙንም አገኘ፤ ከመሠዊያውም «የበራክዩ ልጅ ዘካርያስ ተገደለ!» እያለ የሚጮኽ ድምፅ ሰማ። ደሙም እስኪበቀልለት ድረስ መጮኹን አላቆመም፤ ጌታችን አይሁድን «የገደላችሁት የዘካርያስ ደም ይደርስባችኋል» ያላቸው ለዚህ ነው።

በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ጻድቁ የነቢያት አለቃ ሙሴ አረፈ። ፈርዖን የዕብራውያንን ወንዶች ልጆች ሁሉ እንዲያጠፉ ስላዘዘ ወላጆቹ ወደ ወንዝ ጥለውት ነበር፤ የፈርዖንም ልጅ አግኝታ እንደ ራሷ ልጅ አሳደገችው። አርባ ዓመት ሲሆነው አንድ ግብፃዊ አንድን ዕብራዊ ሲመታ አይቶ ግብፃዊውን ገደለና ወደ ምድያም ሸሸ፤ በሰማንያ ዓመቱም እግዚአብሔር በሚነድ ቍጥቋጦ ውስጥ ሆኖ ተናግሮ የእስራኤልን ልጆች ከግብፅ እንዲያወጣ ላከው። እግዚአብሔር በሙሴ እጅ ግብፅን በዐሥር መቅሠፍቶች መታ፤ ለእስራኤል ቀይ ባሕርን ከፍሎ ፈርዖንንና ሠራዊቱን በውስጡ አሰጠመ፤ በምድረ በዳም አርባ ዓመት ሕዝቡን በመና መገበ፤ ከዐለትም ውኃ አጠጣቸው።

ሕዝቡ ሙሴን ብዙ ጊዜ ቢረግሙትና ሊወግሩት ቢነሡም እጅግ ስለ ወደዳቸው እግዚአብሔርን «የዚህን ሕዝብ ኃጢአት ይቅር ካላልህ ስሜን ከመጽሐፍህ ደምስሰው» ብሎ ለመነ። እግዚአብሔር ሰው ከባልንጀራው ጋር እንደሚነጋገር ከሙሴ ጋር ይነጋገር ነበር፤ የሙሴም ፊት በእግዚአብሔር ክብር ያበራ ነበር። ሙሴ መቶ ሃያ ዓመት በሆነው ጊዜ ሕዝቡን ለደቀ መዝሙሩ ለነዌ ልጅ ለኢያሱ አስረከበ፤ ከዚያም በተራራ ላይ አረፈ። የእስራኤል ልጆች ሥጋውን ወስደው እንዳያመልኩት እግዚአብሔር ሠወረው፤ ሰይጣን ሊገልጠው በፈለገ ጊዜም ሐዋርያው ይሁዳ እንደ መሰከረው ሊቀ መላእክት ሚካኤል ገሠጸው።

በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ የደርሰባ ከተማ ተወላጅ የነበረው ቅዱስ ዲማድዮስ በሰማዕትነት አረፈ። ቤተ ክርስቲያንንና ድሆችን ይወድ፣ በሽተኞችንም ይጐበኝ ነበር፤ ብርሃን የሚያበራ አንድ ሰው ተገልጦለት የሰማዕትነትን አክሊል ሊቀበል እንዲሄድ በነገረው ጊዜም አባቱንና እናቱን፣ ከተማውንም ትቶ ወጣ። በአትሪብ በአገረ ገዥው ፊት በክርስቶስ ማመኑን መሰከረ፤ አገረ ገዥውም ጽኑ ሥቃይ አሠቃይቶ ወደ እስክንድርያው አገረ ገዥ ወደ ሉክያኖስ ላከው። በመርከብ ላይ ሳለ ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ ተገልጦለት የዘለዓለም ደስታን ቃል ገባለት። ሉክያኖስም አሠቃይቶ ራሱን በሰይፍ አስቈረጠው፤ እርሱም በመንግሥተ ሰማያት የሰማዕትነትን አክሊል ተቀበለ። የከተማው ሰዎች ሥጋውን ወስደው አከበሩት፤ በእርሱም ታላላቅ ድንቅና ተአምራት ተደረጉ።
ሰማዕቱ ቅዱስ ሉክዮስም በዚህች ዕለት ይታሰባል። አንድ አገረ ገዥ ደጋግሞ አሠቃየው፤ በመጨረሻም አንገቱን በሰይፍ አስቈረጠው፤ እርሱም የሰማዕትነትን አክሊል ተቀበለ።
ቅዱሳን ኤርምያስና ኤልያኖስ፣ እንዲሁም መነኰሱ አሞን በዚህች ዕለት ይታሰባሉ።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ገዳማዊው ቅዱስ ቂርቆስ አረፈ። ምግቡ የአጋዘን ወተት ነበር፤ በዕረፍቱም ጊዜ ብዙ ተአምራት ተደረጉ።
የቅዱስ ዘካርያስ፣ የነቢዩ ሙሴ፣ የቅዱስ ዲማድዮስ፣ የቅዱስ ሉክዮስ፣ የቅዱሳን ኤርምያስና ኤልያኖስ፣ የአሞንና የቅዱስ ቂርቆስ ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: They were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.

am.verse: ሁለቱም በጌታ ትእዛዝና ሕግጋት ሁሉ ያለነቀፋ እየሄዱ፥ በእግዚአብሔር ፊት ጻድቃን ነበሩ።

title.en: Martyrdom of Abba Bishora, Bishop of Masil
title.am: የመጺል ኤጲስ ቆጶስ የአባ ቢሶራ ሰማዕትነት

en: Abba Bishora, Bishop of Masil, Martyr
St. Fasilides and His Fellow Martyrs
The Miracle of the Archangel Michael at Frumya
King Yasay
am: አባ ቢሶራ የመጺል ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ሰማዕት
ቅዱስ ፋሲለደስና ከእርሱ ጋር የሞቱ ሰማዕታት
የሊቀ መላእክት ቅዱስ ሚካኤል የፍሩምያ ተአምር
ንጉሥ ያሳይ

en: St. Thomas the Apostle
St. Stephen the Protomartyr
Abba Antony the Father of Monks
St. Justina
am: ቅዱስ ቶማስ ሐዋርያ
ቅዱስ እስጢፋኖስ ቀዳሜ ሰማዕት
አባ እንጦንዮስ አበ መነኮሳት
ቅድስት ዮስቴና

en: On this day the Church remembers Abba Bishora, Bishop of Masil, who became a martyr together with three other bishops. We also remember St. Fasilides and the martyrs who died with him, the miracle of the Archangel Michael in the city of Frumya, and the repose of King Yasay.

Abba Bishora was the bishop of Masil, a city in Egypt. When Emperor Diocletian was persecuting the Christians, Bishora longed to shed his blood for the name of Christ. He gathered all his people in front of the sanctuary and taught them every commandment that leads to righteousness, and then he told them what he wished to do. Old and young alike wept and said, “Why are you leaving us? We will not let you go.” They tried to hold him back but could not, and in the end they let him go. He entrusted them to Christ, bade them farewell and set out, while they walked with him, weeping bitterly.

Three bishops named Baskos, Fenabikos and Theodore went with him. They came to the city where the governor lived and confessed their faith in Christ before him, and he tortured them cruelly. When he learned that they were bishops, he made their sufferings even worse, but they endured with great patience, because Christ strengthened them. At last the governor ordered their heads cut off with the sword, and they received the crown of life in the kingdom of heaven. The holy body of Abba Bishora rests to this day in the city of Nasel.
On this day, too, St. Fasilides was martyred together with 14,730 men and seven women.

We also remember a miracle of the Archangel Michael in the city of Frumya in the land of Rome. The church of Michael, the captain of the heavenly hosts, was a place of many wonders and signs. Some Greeks of that region were so consumed with devilish envy that they planned to turn the river's water onto the church and drown it together with its steward. But Michael appeared to the steward, Nartinos, and said, “Be strong and do not be afraid.” He struck a rock with the staff in his hand, and the rock split open and the river's water flowed through it. Those who saw this praised God and honored the Archangel Michael, and to this day the river can be seen flowing through the split rock, never coming near his church.
King Yasay also went to his rest on this day. He completed his struggle on a tree and pleased God.
May the prayers and blessings of Abba Bishora and the bishops martyred with him, St. Fasilides and his companions, the Archangel Michael and King Yasay be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን ከሌሎች ሦስት ኤጲስ ቆጶሳት ጋር በሰማዕትነት ያረፈውን የመጺልን ኤጲስ ቆጶስ አባ ቢሶራን ታስባለች። ቅዱስ ፋሲለደስንና ከእርሱ ጋር የሞቱትን ሰማዕታት፣ ሊቀ መላእክት ቅዱስ ሚካኤል በፍሩምያ ከተማ ያደረገውን ተአምርና የንጉሥ ያሳይን ዕረፍትም እናስባለን።

አባ ቢሶራ በግብፅ የምትገኘው የመጺል ከተማ ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ነበር። ንጉሥ ዲዮቅልጥያኖስ ክርስቲያኖችን ባሳደደ ጊዜ ቢሶራ ስለ ክርስቶስ ስም ደሙን ማፍሰስ ተመኘ። ሕዝቡን ሁሉ በቤተ መቅደሱ ፊት ሰብስቦ ወደ ጽድቅ የሚያደርሱ ትእዛዛትን ሁሉ አስተማራቸው፤ ከዚያም ሊያደርግ የፈለገውን ነገራቸው። ከትልቅ እስከ ትንሽ ሁሉም አለቀሱ፤ «ለምን ትተወናለህ? እኛ እንድትሄድ አንፈቅድልህም» አሉት። ሊያስቀሩት ሞከሩ፤ ነገር ግን አልተቻላቸውም፤ በመጨረሻም ተዉት። እርሱም ለክርስቶስ አደራ ሰጥቷቸው ተሰናብቶ ወጣ፤ እነርሱም መራራ ልቅሶ እያለቀሱ አብረውት ሄዱ።

ቢስኮስ፣ ፊናቢክስና ቴዎድሮስ የተባሉ ሦስት ኤጲስ ቆጶሳት ከእርሱ ጋር ሄዱ። አገረ ገዥው ወደሚኖርበት ከተማ ደርሰው በፊቱ በክርስቶስ ማመናቸውን መሰከሩ፤ እርሱም በጭካኔ አሠቃያቸው። ኤጲስ ቆጶሳት መሆናቸውን ባወቀ ጊዜ ሥቃያቸውን አበዛ፤ እነርሱ ግን ክርስቶስ ስላጸናቸው በታላቅ ትዕግሥት ታገሡ። በመጨረሻም አገረ ገዥው ራሳቸውን በሰይፍ እንዲቆርጧቸው አዘዘ፤ እነርሱም በመንግሥተ ሰማያት የሕይወትን አክሊል ተቀበሉ። የአባ ቢሶራ ቅዱስ ሥጋ እስከ ዛሬ በንሲል ከተማ ያርፋል።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ቅዱስ ፋሲለደስ ከ14,730 ወንዶችና ከሰባት ሴቶች ጋር በሰማዕትነት አረፈ።

በሮም አገር በፍሩምያ ከተማ ሊቀ መላእክት ቅዱስ ሚካኤል ያደረገውን ተአምርም እናስባለን። የሰማይ ሠራዊት አለቃ የሆነው የቅዱስ ሚካኤል ቤተ ክርስቲያን ብዙ ድንቅና ተአምራት የሚታዩባት ነበረች። በዚያ አካባቢ የነበሩ አንዳንድ ግሪኮችም በሰይጣናዊ ቅናት ተሞልተው የወንዙን ውኃ ወደ ቤተ ክርስቲያኑ አዙረው ቤተ ክርስቲያኑን ከመጋቢው ጋር ሊያሰጥሙ አሰቡ። ሚካኤል ግን ለመጋቢው ለናርጢኖስ ተገልጦ «ጽና፤ አትፍራ» አለው። በእጁ በነበረው በትር አንድ ዐለት መታ፤ ዐለቱም ተሰነጠቀ፤ የወንዙም ውኃ በዚያ በኩል አለፈ። ይህን ያዩ ሰዎች እግዚአብሔርን አመሰገኑ፤ ሊቀ መላእክት ሚካኤልንም አከበሩ፤ እስከ ዛሬም ወንዙ በተሰነጠቀው ዐለት ውስጥ ሲያልፍ ይታያል፤ ወደ ቤተ ክርስቲያኑም ከቶ አይቀርብም።
ንጉሥ ያሳይም በዚህች ዕለት አረፈ። እርሱ በዛፍ ላይ ሆኖ ገድሉን የጨረሰና እግዚአብሔርን ደስ ያሰኘ ነው።
የአባ ቢሶራና ከእርሱ ጋር በሰማዕትነት ያረፉት ኤጲስ ቆጶሳት፣ የቅዱስ ፋሲለደስና የባልንጀሮቹ፣ የሊቀ መላእክት ቅዱስ ሚካኤልና የንጉሥ ያሳይ ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

am.verse: መልካም እረኛ እኔ ነኝ። መልካም እረኛ ነፍሱን ስለ በጎቹ ያኖራል።

title.en: The Miracle of Our Lady's Icon at Sedenya
title.am: የእመቤታችን የጼዴንያ ሥዕል ተአምር

en: The Miracle of Our Lady's Icon at Sedenya
The Birth of Our Lady the Virgin Mary
St. Judith the Wise
St. Matronya the Martyr
St. Athanasia and Her Three Children
am: የእመቤታችን የጼዴንያ ሥዕል ተአምር
የእመቤታችን የድንግል ማርያም ልደት
ጥበበኛዋ ቅድስት ዮዲት
ቅድስት መጥሮንያ ሰማዕት
ቅድስት አትናስያና ሦስት ልጆቿ

en: The Holy Cross of Christ
Saints Sergius and Bacchus
St. James the Apostle
St. Tsedale Petros
am: ቅዱስ መስቀለ ክርስቶስ
ቅዱስ ሠርጊስ ወባኮስ
ቅዱስ ያዕቆብ ሐዋርያ
ቅዱስ ጸዳለ ጴጥሮስ

en: On this day the Church remembers the miracle of Our Lady's icon in the city of Sedenya. We also remember the birth of Our Lady the Virgin Mary, the wise Judith, the martyr St. Matronya, and St. Athanasia with her three children.

The icon of Our Lady at Sedenya is said to have been painted by St. Luke the Evangelist. It came to that city because of a widow named Martha, who had made her house a lodging for travelers and loved Our Lady dearly. When a righteous monk named Theodore stayed with her and set out for the holy places in Jerusalem, she asked him to buy her a picture of Our Lady and bring it back. But in Jerusalem he prayed at the holy places and started home without it. Then a voice asked him, “Why did you forget to buy the picture?” So he went back to the market, found a picture of Our Lady with a lovely face and form, bought it and wrapped it in fine cloth.

On the road the picture protected him: when robbers rose up against him, a voice from it said, “Do not be afraid; go on your way,” and when a lion came to attack him, a terrible voice from it drove the lion away. After these wonders Theodore wanted to keep the picture and take it to his own country. But as he was traveling by ship, a great wind carried him to Sedenya, and he went to Martha's house without making himself known. When he tried to slip away the next day, he could not find the way out of the gate, and so it was for three days. At last he told Martha everything and gave her the picture.

When she unwrapped the cloth, Martha found oil dripping from the picture, and for joy she kissed the monk's hands and feet. She placed the icon in her prayer room with great honor, with lamps burning before it day and night and a marble bowl beneath it to catch the oil, and Theodore stayed to serve it for the rest of his life. When the archbishop of that land heard of it, he came with the bishops, the priests and all the people, and they saw that the picture looked as if it were clothed in flesh. They marveled at this divine work. They shared out the oil as a blessing, and at once the bowl filled up again. When they tried to move the icon elsewhere, the earth shook and many fell down in terror. The icon is still in that city today.

Some say that this is also the day Our Lady the Virgin Mary was born. According to the Book of Exposition of Abba Macarius of the monastery of Scete, and another such book from Upper Egypt, the righteous Hanna conceived her on the 17th of Tahsas and gave birth to her on the 10th of Meskerem. The Church tells of her birth more fully on the 1st of Genbot, but it is right to honor it on both days, because she intercedes for us with her beloved Son at all times.
On this day, too, the wise Judith went to her rest. She saved Israel from the wicked Holophernes: she used all her wisdom and resourcefulness until, by the power of God, she cut off his head.

On this day, too, St. Matronya died as a martyr. She was the servant of a Jewish woman, who wanted her to give up her Christian faith and made her work harder when she refused. One day Matronya followed her mistress to the synagogue but turned aside into the church to pray. When her mistress asked why she had not gone in, she answered, “God is far from your synagogue, so how could I enter? The place for me is the holy church, which our Lord Jesus Christ bought with his precious blood.” Furious, the woman beat her and shut her in a dark room for four days without food or drink, then beat her again and locked her up once more, and there Matronya died. Afraid of the judges, her mistress threw the body down from the roof to make it look as if she had fallen by herself. But the wrath of God fell on that woman, and as she came down from the roof she fell and died. Matronya received the crown of martyrdom and went to eternal life.
We also remember St. Athanasia and her three children.
May the prayers and blessings of Our Lady the Virgin Mary, the wise Judith, St. Matronya, and St. Athanasia and her children be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን በጼዴንያ ከተማ የተገለጠውን የእመቤታችንን የሥዕል ተአምር ታስባለች። የእመቤታችን የድንግል ማርያምን ልደት፣ ጥበበኛዋን ዮዲትን፣ ሰማዕቷን ቅድስት መጥሮንያንና ቅድስት አትናስያን ከሦስት ልጆቿ ጋር እናስባለን።

በጼዴንያ ያለችው የእመቤታችን ሥዕል በወንጌላዊው በቅዱስ ሉቃስ እንደ ተሣለች ይነገራል። ወደዚያች ከተማ የመጣችውም ማርታ በተባለች አንዲት መበለት ምክንያት ነው፤ እርሷ ቤቷን ለመንገደኞች ማደሪያ አድርጋ የነበረች ሲሆን እመቤታችንንም እጅግ ትወድ ነበር። ቴዎድሮስ የሚባል አንድ ጻድቅ መነኰስ እርሷ ዘንድ አድሮ በኢየሩሳሌም ወዳሉት ቅዱሳት መካናት ለመሄድ ሲነሣ፣ የእመቤታችንን ሥዕል ገዝቶ እንዲያመጣላት ጠየቀችው። ሆኖም በኢየሩሳሌም በቅዱሳት መካናት ጸልዮ ሥዕሉን ሳይገዛ ወደ አገሩ ተመለሰ። ከዚያም «ሥዕሉን መግዛት ለምን ረሳህ?» የሚል ድምፅ ጠየቀው። ስለዚህ ወደ ገበያ ተመልሶ ፊቷና ቁመናዋ ያማረ የእመቤታችንን ሥዕል አገኘ፤ ገዝቶም በጥሩ ልብስ ጠቀለላት።

በመንገድ ላይ ሥዕሉ ከአደጋ ጠበቀው፤ ወንበዴዎች በተነሡበት ጊዜ ከሥዕሉ «አትፍራ፤ መንገድህን ቀጥል» የሚል ድምፅ ወጣ፤ አንበሳ ሊነጥቀው በመጣም ጊዜ ከሥዕሉ የወጣ አስፈሪ ድምፅ አንበሳውን አባረረው። ቴዎድሮስ እነዚህን ድንቅ ነገሮች ባየ ጊዜ ሥዕሉን ለራሱ አድርጎ ወደ አገሩ ሊወስደው ፈለገ። ነገር ግን በመርከብ ሲጓዝ ታላቅ ነፋስ ወደ ጼዴንያ ወሰደው፤ እርሱም ማንነቱን ሳይገልጥ ወደ ማርታ ቤት ገባ። በማግሥቱ ተሠውሮ ለመውጣት ሲሞክር የበሩን መውጫ አጣ፤ ሦስት ቀንም እንዲሁ ሆነ። በመጨረሻም ለማርታ ሁሉን ነገራት፤ ሥዕሉንም ሰጣት።

ማርታ ልብሱን ስትፈታ ከሥዕሉ ቅባት ሲንጠፈጠፍ አገኘች፤ ከደስታዋም የተነሣ የመነኰሱን እጆችና እግሮች ሳመች። ሥዕሉን በጸሎት ቤቷ ውስጥ በታላቅ ክብር አስቀመጠችው፤ በፊቱ ቀንና ሌሊት የሚበሩ መብራቶችን ሰቀለች፤ ቅባቱን የሚቀበል የዕብነ በረድ ወጭትም ከሥዕሉ በታች አኖረች፤ ቴዎድሮስም እዚያው ቀርቶ በሕይወቱ ዘመን ሁሉ ሥዕሉን አገለገለ። የአገሩ ሊቀ ጳጳሳት ይህን በሰማ ጊዜ ከኤጲስ ቆጶሳቱ፣ ከካህናቱና ከሕዝቡ ሁሉ ጋር መጣ፤ ሥዕሉም ሥጋ የለበሰ እንደሚመስል አዩ። ይህንም አምላካዊ ሥራ አደነቁ። ቅባቱን ለበረከት ተካፈሉ፤ ወጭቱም ወዲያው ተሞላ። ሥዕሉን ወደ ሌላ ቦታ ሊወስዱ ሲሞክሩ ምድር ተናወጠች፤ ብዙዎችም በድንጋጤ ወደቁ። ሥዕሉም እስከ ዛሬ በዚያች ከተማ ይኖራል።

አንዳንዶች ይህች ዕለት እመቤታችን ድንግል ማርያም የተወለደችበትም ቀን ናት ይላሉ። የአስቄጥስ ገዳም አባ መቃርስ በጻፈው መጽሐፈ ግጻዌና በላይኛው ግብፅ በሚገኝ ሌላ መጽሐፍ መሠረት፣ ጻድቋ ሐና እመቤታችንን በታኅሣሥ 17 ቀን ጸነሰቻት፤ በመስከረም 10 ቀን ወለደቻት። ቤተ ክርስቲያን የልደቷን መታሰቢያ በግንቦት 1 ቀን በስፋት ትተርካለች፤ ነገር ግን እርሷ ሁልጊዜ ከተወዳጅ ልጇ ዘንድ ስለ እኛ ስለምትማልድ በሁለቱም ቀን ማክበር ይገባል።
በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ጥበበኛዋ ዮዲት አረፈች። እስራኤልን ከክፉው ከሆሎፎርኒስ አዳነች፤ በእግዚአብሔር ኃይል ራሱን እስክትቈርጥ ድረስ በጥበቧና በብልሃቷ ተጠቀመች።

በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ቅድስት መጥሮንያ በሰማዕትነት አረፈች። እርሷ የአንዲት አይሁዳዊት ሴት አገልጋይ ነበረች፤ እመቤቷም ከክርስትና እምነቷ ሊያስወጣት ትፈልግ ነበር፤ እምቢ ስትል ሥራዋን አከበደችባት። አንድ ቀን መጥሮንያ እመቤቷን ተከትላ ወደ ምኩራብ ሄደች፤ ነገር ግን ዘወር ብላ ለመጸለይ ወደ ቤተ ክርስቲያን ገባች። እመቤቷ ለምን እንዳልገባች ስትጠይቃት «እግዚአብሔር ከምኩራባችሁ ርቋል፤ እንዴት እገባበታለሁ? እኔ የምገባበት ስፍራ ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ በክቡር ደሙ የገዛት ቅድስት ቤተ ክርስቲያን ናት» ስትል መለሰች። ሴትዮዋ ተቆጥታ ደበደበቻት፤ ያለ ምግብና ያለ መጠጥም አራት ቀን በጨለማ ቤት አሰረቻት፤ ከዚያም ደግማ ደበደበቻት፤ እንደገና አሰረቻት፤ በዚያም አረፈች። እመቤቷ ዳኞችን ፈርታ በራሷ ወድቃ የሞተች እንዲመስል በድኗን ከሰገነት ላይ ወደ ታች ጣለችው። ነገር ግን የእግዚአብሔር ቍጣ በዚያች ሴት ላይ ወረደ፤ ከሰገነቱ ስትወርድም ወድቃ ሞተች። መጥሮንያ ግን የሰማዕትነትን አክሊል ተቀዳጅታ ወደ ዘላለማዊ ሕይወት ገባች።
ቅድስት አትናስያንና ሦስቱን ልጆቿንም እናስባለን።
የእመቤታችን የድንግል ማርያም፣ የጥበበኛዋ የዮዲት፣ የቅድስት መጥሮንያ እንዲሁም የቅድስት አትናስያና የልጆቿ ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: for he has looked at the humble state of his servant. For behold, from now on, all generations will call me blessed.

am.verse: የባሪያዪቱን ውርደት ተመልክቷልና። እንሆም፥ ከዛሬ ዠምሮ ትውልድ ሁሉ፦ ብፅዕት ይሉኛል፤

title.en: Martyrdom of St. Fasilides
title.am: የቅዱስ ፋሲለደስ ሰማዕትነት

en: Martyrdom of St. Fasilides
St. Banafzez the Martyr
Saints Sures, Ankityos and Mashadra, Martyrs of Esna
St. Cornelius the Righteous
St. Theodora
Saints Basil, Theodore of Jerusalem and Kawestos
am: የቅዱስ ፋሲለደስ ሰማዕትነት
ቅድስት በነፍዝዝ ሰማዕት
ቅዱሳን ሱርስ፣ አጤኬዎስና መስተሐድራ የእስና ሰማዕታት
ጻድቁ ቆርኔሌዎስ
ቅድስት ታዖድራ
ቅዱሳን ባስልዮስ፣ የኢየሩሳሌሙ ቴዎድሮስና ቀውስጦስ

en: St. Anna Mother of the Virgin Mary
St. Fasilides the Martyr
St. Yared the Hymnographer
Abba Paimon
am: ቅድስት ሐና እመ እግዝእትነ
ቅዱስ ፋሲለደስ ሰማዕት
ቅዱስ ያሬድ ማኅሌታይ
አባ ባይሞን ገዳማዊ

en: On this day the Church remembers the martyrdom of St. Fasilides. We also remember the martyr St. Banafzez, the three farmers of Esna, the righteous Cornelius, St. Theodora, and Saints Basil, Theodore of Jerusalem and Kawestos.

St. Fasilides was a general of the king of Rome and the father and counselor of the kings of Antioch. When King Numerianus died in a war, one of his daughters married Agripada, a goatherd from Upper Egypt who had been put in charge of the royal horses, named him Diocletian and made him king. After a few days he abandoned the God of heaven and earth and worshiped idols. Fasilides gathered his relatives, soldiers and servants and told them that he wanted to shed his blood for Christ, and they all answered, “We will die the same death as you.” They confessed Jesus Christ before Diocletian, who feared them because they belonged to the royal family and sent them away to be punished, each to a different place. Fasilides was sent to Masrus, the governor of the Five Cities of Africa.

Masrus was amazed that Fasilides had given up a kingdom and its glory. Christ sent his angel, who lifted Fasilides up in the spirit to heaven and showed him the dwelling prepared for him, and his soul rejoiced. Then the governor had him cut to pieces with iron rods until he died, but Jesus Christ raised him up unharmed, and the people who saw it believed and were beheaded as martyrs. Fasilides was roasted in an iron pan until his body melted like water and was buried in a deep pit, but Christ raised him a second time, and he stood before Masrus and cried out, “Be ashamed, Masrus, and let your faithless king and your idols be ashamed too! My Lord Jesus Christ has raised me up whole and unharmed.” Again many people believed and died as martyrs.

Masrus then tortured him on a wheel with a saw inside it and on an iron bed over a fire, and there our Lord Jesus Christ appeared to him, raised him up unharmed and promised, “Everyone who keeps your commemoration, or gives alms to the poor in your name, or brings an offering to the church on your feast, whether much or little, I will forgive their sins and give them a home with you in the kingdom of heaven.” At last Masrus, who had no torture left to try, had him beheaded, and Fasilides received the crown of martyrdom in place of the earthly kingdom he had given up. Great wonders appeared at his body, and 23,793 people died as martyrs with him.

On this day, too, the holy woman Banafzez, whose name means “sweet,” died as a martyr. She was very old when she was taken captive, with many other Christians, in the days of Sabor, King of Persia. The commander of the army tortured her cruelly and cut off her head, and the blood from her neck shot far up into the air. Then the strength of the enemies there failed, the light of the sun grew dark, and a sweet fragrance filled the place.

The three farmers Sures, Ankityos and Mashadra of Esna also became martyrs. Arianus had been killing people everywhere, sparing no one, until his soldiers were so exhausted that they put their swords away. The three farmers, coming back from the field, met him and cried out boldly, “We are Christians!” Arianus told his soldiers to kill them, but they answered that they were too tired. “Here are our digging tools,” said the farmers. “Kill us with them.” They laid their necks on a stone, and the soldiers cut off their heads.

On this day we also remember the repose of Cornelius, an army commander and a righteous man in the days of the apostles. An angel told him to send for the apostle Peter, who came and taught him the word of God, and Cornelius believed and was baptized with all his household. Peter ordained him a priest for Alexandria, a city full of idol worship, where he taught and baptized many, including the governor Demetrius and his household. Cornelius completed his apostolic labors and died in peace; he was the first of the Gentiles to believe.

On this day, too, St. Theodora of Alexandria died, in the days of the emperor Zeno. After a man wronged her, she was overcome with grief, put on men's clothes, secretly left the city, called herself Theodore, and joined a monastery of monks, who all took her for a eunuch. For many years she endured hunger, thirst and long vigils. Then a young woman who had become pregnant by another man falsely named Theodore as the father, and her parents brought the baby to the abbot. Not knowing that Theodore was a woman, he scolded her for shaming the monks, and she answered only, “I have sinned; have mercy on me, Father.” Angrily he gave her the child and drove her out, and she lived seven years in the desert with the boy, enduring many torments from devils. At last she was taken back into the monastery, and a few days later she died in peace and received eternal life.
We also remember the martyr St. Basil, Theodore, Bishop of Jerusalem, and Kawestos, the chief of the martyrs.
May the prayers and blessings of St. Fasilides, St. Banafzez, Saints Sures, Ankityos and Mashadra, St. Cornelius, St. Theodora, and Saints Basil, Theodore and Kawestos be with us all. Amen.
am: በዚህች ዕለት ቤተ ክርስቲያን የቅዱስ ፋሲለደስን ሰማዕትነት ታስባለች። ሰማዕቷን ቅድስት በነፍዝዝን፣ የእስና አገር ሦስት ገበሬዎችን፣ ጻድቁን ቆርኔሌዎስን፣ ቅድስት ታዖድራንና ቅዱሳን ባስልዮስን፣ የኢየሩሳሌሙን ቴዎድሮስንና ቀውስጦስንም እናስባለን።

ቅዱስ ፋሲለደስ የሮም ንጉሥ የጦር አለቃ፣ የአንጾኪያም ነገሥታት አባትና መካሪ ነበር። ንጉሥ ኑማርያኖስ በጦርነት በሞተ ጊዜ ከሴቶች ልጆቹ አንዷ በንጉሥ ፈረሶች ላይ ተሹሞ የነበረውን የላይኛው ግብፅ ተወላጅ የፍየል እረኛ አግሪጳዳን አገባችው፤ ዲዮቅልጥያኖስ ብላም ሰይማ አነገሠችው። እርሱም ከጥቂት ቀን በኋላ ሰማይንና ምድርን የፈጠረውን አምላክ ትቶ ጣዖታትን ማምለክ ጀመረ። ፋሲለደስ ዘመዶቹን፣ ወታደሮቹንና አገልጋዮቹን ሰብስቦ ስለ ክርስቶስ ደሙን ሊያፈስ እንደሚፈልግ ነገራቸው፤ እነርሱም ሁሉ «አንተ የምትሞትበትን ሞት እኛም አብረን እንሞታለን» አሉት። በዲዮቅልጥያኖስ ፊት ቆመው ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስን መሰከሩ፤ እርሱም የንጉሣዊ ቤተሰብ አባላት ስለ ነበሩ ፈራቸው፤ ሊያሠቃዩአቸውም እያንዳንዳቸውን ወደ ተለያየ ቦታ ሰደዳቸው። ፋሲለደስንም የአፍሪካ አምስት ከተሞች አገረ ገዥ ወደ ሆነው ወደ መጽሩስ ላከው።

መጽሩስ ፋሲለደስ መንግሥቱንና ክብሩን መተዉን አይቶ እጅግ ተደነቀ። ክርስቶስ መልአኩን ላከ፤ መልአኩም ፋሲለደስን በመንፈስ ወደ ሰማይ አሳርጎ ተዘጋጅቶለት የነበረውን መኖሪያ አሳየው፤ ነፍሱም በደስታ ተሞላች። ከዚያም አገረ ገዥው በብረት ዘንግ ሥጋውን እየቆራረጠ እስኪሞት አሠቃየው፤ ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ ግን ያለ ጉዳት አስነሣው፤ ይህን ያዩ ሰዎችም አምነው በሰይፍ ተቈርጠው ሰማዕት ሆኑ። ፋሲለደስ በብረት ምጣድ ውስጥ ሥጋው እንደ ውኃ እስኪቀልጥ ድረስ ተጠበሰ፤ ጥልቅ ጕድጓድ ውስጥም ተቀበረ፤ ክርስቶስ ግን ለሁለተኛ ጊዜ አስነሣው፤ እርሱም በመጽሩስ ፊት ቆሞ «መጽሩስ ሆይ፣ እፈር፤ ከሀዲው ንጉሥህና ጣዖታትህም ይፈሩ! ጌታዬ ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ ሳይጎዳ ደኅና አድርጎ አስነሥቶኛል» ብሎ ጮኸ። ዳግመኛም ብዙ ሰዎች አምነው ሰማዕት ሆኑ።

መጽሩስ ከዚያ በኋላ በውስጡ መጋዝ ባለው መንኰራኵርና በብረት አልጋ ላይ ከበታቹ እሳት እያነደደ አሠቃየው፤ በዚያም ጌታችን ኢየሱስ ክርስቶስ ተገለጠለት፤ ያለ ጉዳትም አስነሣው፤ እንዲህም ሲል ቃል ገባለት፦ «መታሰቢያህን የሚያደርግ፣ በስምህ ለድሆች የሚመጸውት፣ ወይም በበዓልህ ቀን ለቤተ ክርስቲያን መባ የሚያቀርብ ሁሉ፣ ብዙም ይሁን ጥቂት፣ ኃጢአቱን ይቅር እላለሁ፤ በመንግሥተ ሰማያትም ከአንተ ጋር የሚኖርበትን ስፍራ እሰጠዋለሁ።» በመጨረሻም መጽሩስ የሚያሠቃይበት ሌላ ዘዴ ስላልቀረው ፋሲለደስን በሰይፍ አስቈረጠው፤ ፋሲለደስም ትቶት በነበረው ምድራዊ መንግሥት ፋንታ የሰማዕትነትን አክሊል ተቀበለ። ከሥጋውም ብዙ ድንቅ ተአምራት ታዩ፤ ከእርሱም ጋር 23,793 ሰዎች በሰማዕትነት አረፉ።

በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ ስሟ «ጣፋጭ» ማለት የሆነች ቅድስት በነፍዝዝ በሰማዕትነት አረፈች። እርሷ እጅግ አርጅታ ነበር፤ በፋርስ ንጉሥ በሳቦር ዘመን ከሌሎች ብዙ ክርስቲያኖች ጋር ተማርካ ተወሰደች። የሠራዊቱ አለቃ ክፉኛ አሠቃይቶ ራሷን ቈረጠ፤ ከአንገቷም የፈሰሰው ደም ወደ ላይ ርቆ ተረጨ። በዚያም የነበሩ ጠላቶች ብርታታቸው ተሰበረ፤ የፀሐይ ብርሃን ጨለመ፤ ጣፋጭ መዓዛም ቦታውን ሞላው።

የእስና አገር ሦስት ገበሬዎች ሱርስ፣ አጤኬዎስና መስተሐድራም በሰማዕትነት አረፉ። አርያኖስ ማንንም ሳያስቀር በየስፍራው ሰዎችን ይገድል ነበር፤ በመጨረሻም ወታደሮቹ ከድካማቸው የተነሣ ሰይፋቸውን ወደ ሰገባ መለሱ። ሦስቱ ገበሬዎች ከእርሻ ሲመለሱ አገኙትና «እኛ ክርስቲያኖች ነን!» ብለው በድፍረት ጮኹ። አርያኖስ ወታደሮቹን እነርሱን እንዲገድሉ አዘዛቸው፤ እነርሱ ግን እንደደከሙ ነገሩት። ገበሬዎቹም «እነሆ መቆፈሪያዎቻችን፤ በእነርሱ ግደሉን» አሉ። አንገታቸውን በድንጋይ ላይ አኖሩ፤ ወታደሮቹም ራሳቸውን ቈረጡ።

በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ በሐዋርያት ዘመን የነበረውን የጦር አለቃና ጻድቅ ሰው የቆርኔሌዎስን ዕረፍት እናስባለን። መልአክ ሐዋርያውን ጴጥሮስን እንዲያስጠራ ነገረው፤ ጴጥሮስም መጥቶ የእግዚአብሔርን ቃል አስተማረው፤ ቆርኔሌዎስም አምኖ ከቤተሰቡ ሁሉ ጋር ተጠመቀ። ጴጥሮስ ለእስክንድርያ ካህን አድርጎ ሾመው፤ እስክንድርያ በጣዖት አምልኮ የተሞላች ከተማ ነበረች፤ በዚያም ብዙዎችን አስተምሮ አጠመቀ፤ ከእነርሱም መካከል አገረ ገዥው ድሜጥሮስና ቤተሰቡ ነበሩ። ቆርኔሌዎስ ሐዋርያዊ ተጋድሎውን ፈጽሞ በሰላም አረፈ፤ ከአሕዛብ ያመነ የመጀመሪያው እርሱ ነው።

በዚህች ዕለት ደግሞ በንጉሥ ዘይኑን ዘመን የእስክንድርያዋ ቅድስት ታዖድራ አረፈች። አንድ ሰው በደላት፤ እርሷም በኀዘን ተሞላች፤ የወንዶች ልብስ ለብሳ በስውር ከከተማዋ ወጣች፤ ስሟን ቴዎድሮስ ብላ ሰይማ ወንዶች መነኰሳት ወዳሉበት ገዳም ገባች፤ ሁሉም ጃንደረባ እንደ ሆነች ያስቡ ነበር። ለብዙ ዓመታት ረሃብን፣ ጥምንና ረጅም የሌሊት ጸሎትን ታገሠች። በኋላም አንዲት ወጣት ከሌላ ሰው ጸንሳ በሐሰት አባቱ ቴዎድሮስ ነው አለች፤ ወላጆቿም ሕፃኑን ወደ አበ ምኔቱ ወሰዱት። አበ ምኔቱ ሴት መሆኗን ሳያውቅ መነኰሳቱን ስላሳፈረች ገሠጻት፤ እርሷም «አባቴ ሆይ፣ ኃጢአት ሠርቻለሁ፤ ማረኝ» ብቻ አለች። ተቈጥቶ ሕፃኑን ሰጥቷት ከገዳሙ አባረራት፤ እርሷም ከሕፃኑ ጋር ሰባት ዓመት በበረሃ ኖረች፤ ከአጋንንትም ብዙ ሥቃይ ደረሰባት። በመጨረሻም ተመልሳ ወደ ገዳሙ ገባች፤ ከጥቂት ቀንም በኋላ በሰላም አርፋ የዘላለም ሕይወትን ተቀበለች።
የሰማዕቱን ቅዱስ ባስልዮስን፣ የኢየሩሳሌሙን ኤጲስ ቆጶስ ቴዎድሮስንና የሰማዕታቱን አለቃ ቀውስጦስንም እናስባለን።
የቅዱስ ፋሲለደስ፣ የቅድስት በነፍዝዝ፣ የቅዱሳን ሱርስ፣ አጤኬዎስና መስተሐድራ፣ የቅዱስ ቆርኔሌዎስ፣ የቅድስት ታዖድራ እንዲሁም የቅዱሳን ባስልዮስ፣ ቴዎድሮስና ቀውስጦስ ጸሎትና በረከት ከሁላችን ጋር ይሁን። አሜን።

en.verse: Don’t be afraid of the things which you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested; and you will have oppression for ten days. Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life.

am.verse: ልትቀበለው ያለህን መከራ አትፍራ። እንሆ፥ እንድትፈተኑ ዲያብሎስ ከእናንተ አንዳንዶቻችሁን በወህኒ ሊያገባችሁ አለው፥ ዐሥር ቀንም መከራን ትቀበላላችሁ። እስከ ሞት ድረስ የታመንህ ሁን የሕይወትንም አክሊል እሰጥሃለሁ።

title.en: Feast of the Archangel Michael and the Council of Ephesus
title.am: የሊቀ መላእክት የቅዱስ ሚካኤል በዓል እና የኤፌሶን ጉባኤ

en: Feast of the Archangel Michael
The Council of Ephesus (Two Hundred Bishops)
St. Aflahos the Martyr and His Companions
Saints Luyuras and Calanicus, Martyrs
Joachim and Hanna
Feast of St. Stephen in Rome
am: የሊቀ መላእክት የቅዱስ ሚካኤል በዓል
የኤፌሶን ጉባኤ (የሁለት መቶ ኤጲስ ቆጶሳት)
ቅዱስ አፍላሆስ ሰማዕትና ባልንጀሮቹ
ቅዱሳን ሉዩራስና ባሌኒኮስ ሰማዕታት
ኢያቄምና ሐና
የቅዱስ እስጢፋኖስ በዓል በሮም

en: Archangel Michael
St. John Chrysostom
Abba Samuel of Mount Qalmon
am: ቅዱስ ሚካኤል ሊቀ መላእክት
ቅዱስ ዮሐንስ አፈወርቅ
አባ ሳሙኤል ዘደብረ ቀልሞን

en: On this day the Church keeps the feast of the Archangel Michael. We also remember the council of two hundred bishops at Ephesus, the martyr St. Aflahos and his companions, the martyrs Luyuras and Calanicus, Joachim and Hanna, and St. Stephen.

On this day God sent the glorious archangel Michael to the prophet Isaiah, the son of Amoz, and showed mercy to King Hezekiah of Judah. Isaiah was to go to Hezekiah and tell him that God had healed him of his sickness and added fifteen years to his life. In those years Hezekiah took a wife and became the father of Manasseh.

On this day, too, two hundred holy bishops gathered in the city of Ephesus. This was the third of the great councils of the Church, and it met in the twentieth year of the reign of Theodosius the Younger, the son of Arcadius and grandson of Theodosius the Great. The bishops came together because of the error of Nestorius, the Archbishop of Constantinople. He taught that our Lady the Virgin Mary did not give birth to God in the flesh but to a mere man, in whom the Son of God afterwards came to dwell, not united with him but dwelling in him only by his own choice. So, Nestorius said, Christ has two natures.

The fathers debated with Nestorius and showed him that the one born of the holy Virgin Mary was God who had become man. They reminded him of the words of the angel Gabriel to our Lady in the Gospel of Luke, that the child to be born of her would be called the Son of the Most High, and of the prophecy of Isaiah: “Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel.” They added another prophecy, that from the line of Jesse would come the hope of the nations. Then St. Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria, rebuked and counseled Nestorius, saying, “Once the natures have become one in union, they cannot be separated; we believe and declare that the Word of God who became man is one nature.”

But Nestorius would not turn from his unbelief. The whole council rebuked him and warned that he would lose his priesthood and his office unless he gave up his evil teaching. He would not listen, so they removed him from his office, anathematized him, cut him off from the Church and drove him out. He went to Upper Egypt, where he died a terrible death.
